```{r setup}
#| label: setup
library(dplyr)
library(here)
library(stringr)
library(yaml)

source(here::here("factsheets", "_generate", "R", "factsheet-functions.R"))

# Editable intro text + citations for every factsheet. The prose is edited in
# docs/factsheet-prose.docx and converted into content/factsheet-content.yml by
# scripts/prose_docx_to_yml.R; the YAML is a generated file, not a source one.
# Everything else (maps, tables, tiers) is computed from the live pipeline data.
content <- fs_load_content()

# Output directory for regenerated factsheets. Writes to a PREVIEW folder so the
# original /factsheets/*.html files stay untouched for side-by-side comparison.
out_dir <- here::here("factsheets", "_generate", "_preview")
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

# Purpose

This document builds the ADA-PARC national factsheets as HTML files in a
reproducible, source-controlled generator. Rendering it (a) writes factsheet
HTML into `_preview/` and (b) produces this validation report. Reviewed files
are promoted to `www/factsheets/` with `scripts/promote_factsheets.R`; nothing
here writes to the published directory.

Four of the sheets were originally reverse-engineered from hand-built PDFs
published in September 2025 from the **2019–2023 ACS 5-year** vintage (and, for
HCBS, a CMS/Mathematica LTSS spreadsheet). The data now in the pipeline
(`data/final/national_data.Rds`) is a later vintage, so regenerated values
differ from the published snapshot. This is the intended behavior for future
updates: bump the source data and regenerate.

**Living in Community** and **Living in Institution** are new, built for the
revised ten-sheet structure. Living in Institution absorbs and replaces the
September 2025 nursing home sheet, and corrects its denominator; see the note
under Community Living below, and `docs/factsheets_audit.qmd` for the wider
plan.

**Technology Access** is the tenth and last, added 7 August 2026. It was held
back from the July build because its source could not be reproduced, and it is
built here on the PUMS rebuild described in `docs/tech-access-rebuild-plan.qmd`.
It is the only sheet not drawn from published ACS summary tables, which changes
its population; see its own section at the foot of this document.

## Methodology

Tiers are equal-count quartiles via `quantile(type = 7)` + `findInterval`, with
per-indicator direction:

| Factsheet             | Indicator(s)                                  | Direction        | Scale       |
|-----------------------|-----------------------------------------------|------------------|-------------|
| Living in Community   | % PWD in the community; at home               | high = Excellent | single      |
| Living in Community   | % PWD in non-institutional group quarters     | magnitude only   | single      |
| Living in Institution | % PWD institutional; nursing; correctional    | low = Excellent  | single      |
| HCBS                  | community-living spending per recipient       | high = Excellent | single      |
| Housing               | % HoH w/ disability (PH; HCV)                 | high = Excellent | per-map     |
| Poverty               | % below poverty, all ages + 3 age bands       | low = Excellent  | per-map     |
| Technology Access     | % PWD w/ computer; internet; smartphone       | high = Excellent | per-map     |

"Magnitude only" means the map keeps the four-color sequential ramp but drops
the Excellent/Poor labeling, because the indicator has no defensible better or
worse direction. See `FS_TIER_LABELS_MAGNITUDE` in `R/factsheet-functions.R`.

Scope is 50 states + DC (USA and Puerto Rico excluded). Two sheets carry Puerto
Rico in their tables where a figure exists, Housing and Technology Access, and
neither puts it on a map or lets it move the quartile breaks.

```{r load-data}
#| label: load-data
national <- readRDS(here::here("data", "final", "national_data.Rds"))

# 50 states + DC, ordered for joins.
states_df <- national |>
  filter(!ABBR %in% c("USA", "PR")) |>
  mutate(fips = unname(FS_ABBR_TO_FIPS[ABBR]))

stopifnot(nrow(states_df) == 51, all(!is.na(states_df$fips)))
acs_year <- unique(national$year)
acs_year
```

# Community Living: shared derived measures

Every Community Living measure is calculated against the same denominator, the
total population with a disability (`pop_grp_total_dis`), so the residence
categories form an exact partition:

$$\text{living at home} + \text{non-institutional group quarters} + \text{institutional} = 100\%$$

and the institutional share decomposes again into nursing and medical
facilities, adult correctional facilities, and a small residual covering
settings such as psychiatric hospitals and juvenile facilities.

That matters for two reasons. First, the institutional total has **no variable
of its own** in `dict_vars.csv`; the row that should hold it has a populated
`var_pretty` and a blank `var_readable`. Deriving it as the residual gives an
exact figure with no pipeline change. Second, it makes the two Community Living
sheets exact complements of one another, which is what lets *Living in
Community* and *Living in Institution* be read together.

`fs_cl_measures()` performs the derivation and refuses to return if the
partition does not hold, so a future vintage with changed variable definitions
fails at build time rather than publishing a decomposition that does not add up.

## A note on the nursing home denominator

The nursing home fact sheet published in September 2025, which *Living in
Institution* replaces, calculated its rate as
`pop_grp_nursing_18to64_dis / pop_cni_18to64_all`. That denominator is the
civilian **noninstitutional** population, which excludes the people counted in
the numerator, and it does not match the definition the sheet itself described
("state percentages for working-age people with disabilities"). It produced
rates around 0.14% where the correct base gives around 1.13%, and because the
two series correlate only at 0.83, tier assignments differ as well.

The sheets below use the total population with a disability throughout. This is
a deliberate correction. It is documented internally, in `docs/factsheets_audit.qmd`
and in `factsheets/old/retired-2026-07-28/README.md`, rather than on the sheet;
the client asked for the explanatory box to come off the published version.

```{r cl-data}
#| label: cl-data
cl <- states_df |>
  fs_cl_measures() |>
  mutate(
    name = NAME,
    cl_community_n_dis = pop_grp_home_dis + pop_grp_noninstgroupquarters_total_dis,
    # Direction per indicator. Non-institutional group quarters is deliberately
    # "magnitude" rather than high_good: the Census category mixes group homes
    # and supported living with emergency shelters and college dormitories, so
    # neither end of the range is a better outcome. Its map keeps the same
    # sequential color ramp but drops the Excellent/Poor labeling.
    tier_community   = fs_assign_tiers(cl_community_dis,   "high_good"),
    tier_home        = fs_assign_tiers(cl_home_dis,        "high_good"),
    tier_nonintgq    = fs_assign_tiers(cl_nonintgq_dis,    "magnitude"),
    tier_inst        = fs_assign_tiers(cl_inst_dis,        "low_good"),
    tier_nursing     = fs_assign_tiers(cl_nursing_dis,     "low_good"),
    tier_corrections = fs_assign_tiers(cl_corrections_dis, "low_good")
  )

# ---- pooled PWD/PWOD tiers for the simplified template (2026-09-01) ----------
# Each Community Living indicator becomes its own single-indicator sheet with a
# comparative PWD/PWOD dual map on ONE scale pooled across disability status.
# Group quarters keeps its "magnitude" framing (no better/worse direction), so
# it pools like high_good (darkest = highest share) but its labels read
# "Highest quarter" through "Lowest quarter".
cl_pooled <- list(
  community = fs_tier_breaks(c(cl$cl_community_dis,   cl$cl_community_nodis)),
  home      = fs_tier_breaks(c(cl$cl_home_dis,        cl$cl_home_nodis)),
  gq        = fs_tier_breaks(c(cl$cl_nonintgq_dis,    cl$cl_nonintgq_nodis)),
  inst      = fs_tier_breaks(c(cl$cl_inst_dis,        cl$cl_inst_nodis)),
  nursing   = fs_tier_breaks(c(cl$cl_nursing_dis,     cl$cl_nursing_nodis)),
  corr      = fs_tier_breaks(c(cl$cl_corrections_dis, cl$cl_corrections_nodis))
)
cl <- cl |>
  mutate(
    ptier_community_dis = fs_assign_tiers(cl_community_dis,   "high_good", breaks = cl_pooled$community),
    ptier_community_nod = fs_assign_tiers(cl_community_nodis, "high_good", breaks = cl_pooled$community),
    ptier_home_dis      = fs_assign_tiers(cl_home_dis,        "high_good", breaks = cl_pooled$home),
    ptier_home_nod      = fs_assign_tiers(cl_home_nodis,      "high_good", breaks = cl_pooled$home),
    ptier_gq_dis        = fs_assign_tiers(cl_nonintgq_dis,    "magnitude", breaks = cl_pooled$gq),
    ptier_gq_nod        = fs_assign_tiers(cl_nonintgq_nodis,  "magnitude", breaks = cl_pooled$gq),
    ptier_inst_dis      = fs_assign_tiers(cl_inst_dis,        "low_good",  breaks = cl_pooled$inst),
    ptier_inst_nod      = fs_assign_tiers(cl_inst_nodis,      "low_good",  breaks = cl_pooled$inst),
    ptier_nursing_dis   = fs_assign_tiers(cl_nursing_dis,     "low_good",  breaks = cl_pooled$nursing),
    ptier_nursing_nod   = fs_assign_tiers(cl_nursing_nodis,   "low_good",  breaks = cl_pooled$nursing),
    ptier_corr_dis      = fs_assign_tiers(cl_corrections_dis, "low_good",  breaks = cl_pooled$corr),
    ptier_corr_nod      = fs_assign_tiers(cl_corrections_nodis,"low_good", breaks = cl_pooled$corr)
  )

# Population-weighted national shares. The introductions in
# docs/factsheet-prose.docx quote these figures as typed text, so they must be
# checked against this output whenever the data vintage changes.
cl_national <- tibble::tibble(
  measure = c("Living at home", "Non-institutional group quarters",
              "Living in community", "Living in an institution",
              "  nursing / medical facility", "  correctional facility",
              "  other institutional"),
  pwd = c(
    sum(cl$pop_grp_home_dis), sum(cl$pop_grp_noninstgroupquarters_total_dis),
    sum(cl$cl_community_n_dis), sum(cl$cl_inst_n_dis),
    sum(cl$cl_nursing_n_dis), sum(cl$pop_grp_corrections_total_dis),
    sum(cl$cl_other_inst_n_dis)) / sum(cl$pop_grp_total_dis) * 100,
  no_disability = c(
    sum(cl$pop_grp_home_nodis), sum(cl$pop_grp_noninstgroupquarters_total_nodis),
    sum(cl$pop_grp_home_nodis) + sum(cl$pop_grp_noninstgroupquarters_total_nodis),
    sum(cl$cl_inst_n_nodis), sum(cl$cl_nursing_n_nodis),
    sum(cl$pop_grp_corrections_total_nodis),
    sum(cl$cl_other_inst_n_nodis)) / sum(cl$pop_grp_total_nodis) * 100)

cl_national |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

```{r economic-template}
#| label: economic-template
# Shared assembler for the simplified single-indicator template (2026-09-01):
# takeaway, comparative PWD/PWOD dual map on one pooled scale, Why This Matters
# with Key Numbers and a best/worst spotlight, an explainer, and the searchable
# ranked table. Used by the three Employment split sheets and the Poverty
# all-ages lead. Secondary indicators (the three Poverty age bands) reuse
# fs_dual_map() + fs_ranked_table() directly without the Why This Matters block.
build_dual_sheet <- function(spec, data, acs_year) {
  dm <- if (isTRUE(spec$map$single)) fs_single_map(spec$map, data)
        else fs_dual_map(spec$map, data)
  rt <- fs_ranked_table(spec$ranked, data)

  why_html  <- paste0("      <p>", unlist(spec$why_matters), "</p>", collapse = "\n")
  expl_html <- paste0("      <p>", unlist(spec$explainer),   "</p>", collapse = "\n")

  # HCBS carries a {source_year} token in its footnotes and About box.
  about <- spec$about
  if (!is.null(about))
    about$body <- fs_fill_years(about$body, source_year = spec$source_year)

  # Optional trailing content (Poverty appends its three light age-band sections
  # here, between the lead indicator's ranked table and the footnotes).
  tail_html <- spec$tail_html %||% ""
  tail_js   <- spec$tail_js %||% ""

  main_html <- paste0(
"\n",
fs_population_note(spec$population_note$note, spec$population_note$detail),
fs_takeaway(spec$takeaway),
dm$html, "\n",
'    <section class="why-matters" aria-label="Why this matters">
      <h2 class="section-heading">Why This Matters</h2>
', why_html, '
', fs_key_numbers(spec$key_numbers), '
', fs_spotlight(spec$spotlight$best, spec$spotlight$worst), '
    </section>

    <h2 class="section-heading">', spec$explainer_heading, '</h2>
    <div class="explainer">
', expl_html, '
    </div>

', rt$html, '

', tail_html, '

', if (!is.null(about)) fs_about(about) else "", '

', fs_footnotes(spec$footnotes, acs_year = acs_year,
               source_year = spec$source_year, pums_year = spec$pums_year), '
')

  head_html <- fs_html_head(
    title = spec$page_title, description = spec$page_desc,
    extra_css = fs_read_asset("factsheet-template.css"))
  header_html <- fs_header(spec$header_title, spec$header_subtitle, spec$header_eyebrow)

  path <- file.path(out_dir, spec$out_file)
  fs_write_file(
    path = path, head_html = head_html, header_html = header_html,
    main_html = main_html, footer_html = fs_footer(),
    scripts_html = fs_scripts(paste0(dm$js, "\n\n", rt$js, "\n\n", tail_js),
                              extra_assets = "factsheet-ranked-table.js"))
  path
}

# A secondary indicator under the simplified template: the comparative dual map
# and its ranked table, but none of the Why This Matters furniture. Used for the
# three Poverty age bands. `lead` is an optional section-intro paragraph.
fs_light_dual <- function(map_spec, ranked_spec, data, lead = NULL) {
  dm <- fs_dual_map(map_spec, data)
  rt <- fs_ranked_table(ranked_spec, data)
  lead_html <- if (!is.null(lead) && nzchar(paste(unlist(lead), collapse = "")))
    paste0('    <p class="section-intro">',
           paste(unlist(lead), collapse = " "), "</p>\n") else ""
  list(html = paste0(lead_html, dm$html, "\n", rt$html, "\n"),
       js   = paste0(dm$js, "\n\n", rt$js))
}

# Generic single-indicator dual-map sheet assembler. Used by every Community
# Living and Community Participation split sheet. `key_numbers` and `spot_labels`
# are supplied by the caller (the parts that vary by indicator); everything else
# is derived.
#
# THE MAP AND THE TIER COLUMN SHOW DIFFERENT THINGS, DELIBERATELY (2026-09-02).
# The two map panels are shaded on one scale POOLED across disability status, so
# the gap between the panels reads straight off the colour. That pooled scale
# pushes the with-disability panel almost entirely into the bottom bands on many
# indicators, which would make the ranked table's Tier column carry two labels
# for fifty-one states. So the Tier column instead ranks each state WITHIN the
# with-disability population (`rank_tier_col`, a self-ranked tier computed with
# no pooled breaks). The ranked-table intro and note say so.
cp_eyebrow <- "ADA-PARC &middot; Community Participation"
cp_read_shared <- paste0(
  "Both maps use one colour scale, so a shade means the same rate on either ",
  "map. The four bands are cut on the two populations pooled. Hover or tab ",
  "through either map for a state's exact figure. ")

cp_pts_card <- function(a, b, label) list(
  number = paste0(formatC(abs(a - b), format = "f", digits = 1), " pts"),
  label = label, gap = TRUE)
# The "x as likely" card. The multiple is taken from the two rates AS ROUNDED
# for display (via `fmt`), so it reconciles with the two rate cards it sits
# beside instead of being computed from more precision than the sheet shows.
# Only use where the denominator is comfortably above zero; where it rounds to
# nothing (e.g. nursing homes) use cp_pts_card instead.
cp_ratio_card <- function(hi, lo, label, fmt = function(x) fmt_pct(x, 1)) {
  num <- function(s) as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", s))
  list(number = paste0(formatC(num(fmt(hi)) / num(fmt(lo)),
                               format = "f", digits = 1), "&times;"),
       label = label, gap = TRUE)
}

build_split_sheet <- function(id, out_file, title, subtitle, key, data,
                              dis_col, nod_col, ptier_dis, ptier_nod, rank_tier_col,
                              direction, pooled_breaks,
                              pop_note, pop_detail, value_label, unit_word,
                              key_numbers, spot_labels, acs_year, src,
                              magnitude = FALSE, pums_year = NULL, extra_why = NULL,
                              value_fmt = NULL,
                              eyebrow = "ADA-PARC &middot; Community Participation") {
  vf  <- value_fmt %||% function(x) fmt_pct(x, 1)
  o   <- if (direction == "low_good") order(data[[dis_col]]) else order(-data[[dis_col]])
  best <- data[o[1], ]; worst <- data[o[nrow(data)], ]
  tl  <- if (magnitude) "magnitude" else "performance"
  leg <- if (magnitude) list(b = NULL, w = NULL) else
    (if (direction == "low_good") list(b = "lowest rate", w = "highest rate")
     else list(b = "highest rate", w = "lowest rate"))
  cfg <- content[[key]]

  rank_word <- if (magnitude)
    "the Tier column below ranks each state's quarter among states with a disability"
  else
    "the Tier column below ranks each state among states with a disability"

  spec <- list(
    id = id, out_file = out_file,
    page_title = paste0(title, " | ADA-PARC Fact Sheet"),
    page_desc = paste0("ADA-PARC fact sheet on ", tolower(title),
      " among people with disabilities, with state-by-state data."),
    header_title = title, header_eyebrow = eyebrow, header_subtitle = subtitle,
    population_note = list(note = pop_note, detail = pop_detail),
    takeaway = cfg$takeaway,
    why_matters = c(cfg$intro, extra_why),
    explainer = cfg[[grep("_lead$", names(cfg), value = TRUE)[1]]],
    explainer_heading = "What This Map Measures",
    key_numbers = key_numbers,
    spotlight = list(
      best = list(label = spot_labels[1], state = best$name,
        value = paste0(vf(best[[dis_col]]), " ", unit_word),
        note = paste0("Against ", vf(best[[nod_col]]),
          " of people without disabilities in the same state.")),
      worst = list(label = spot_labels[2], state = worst$name,
        value = paste0(vf(worst[[dis_col]]), " ", unit_word),
        note = paste0("Against ", vf(worst[[nod_col]]),
          " of people without disabilities in the same state."))),
    map = list(
      id = id, map_title = paste0(title, ": People With and Without Disabilities"),
      dis_col = dis_col, nod_col = nod_col,
      tier_dis_col = ptier_dis, tier_nod_col = ptier_nod,
      direction = direction, tier_labels = tl, fmt = vf,
      value_label = value_label, pooled_breaks = pooled_breaks,
      # Only override the legend-range formatter when the caller supplied a
      # custom value formatter (e.g. adaptive sub-1% precision on nursing homes);
      # every other sheet keeps the default one-decimal ranges unchanged.
      range_fmt = if (!is.null(value_fmt)) vf else NULL,
      legend_best = leg$b, legend_worst = leg$w,
      svg_title_dis = paste0(title, ", people with disabilities, by U.S. state"),
      svg_desc_dis = paste0("Choropleth of the 50 states and DC shaded by the ",
        tolower(value_label), " among people with disabilities, on a scale ",
        "shared with the map for people without disabilities. Full data is in ",
        "the table below."),
      svg_title_nod = paste0(title, ", people without disabilities, by U.S. state"),
      svg_desc_nod = paste0("Choropleth of the 50 states and DC on the same ",
        "shared scale for people without disabilities. Full data is in the ",
        "table below."),
      caption = paste0(cp_read_shared, src)),
    ranked = list(
      id = id, section_heading = paste0(title, ", by State"),
      intro = paste0("Every state and DC, ranked by the ", tolower(value_label),
        " among people with disabilities. The maps above are shaded on one scale ",
        "pooled with people without disabilities; ", rank_word, "."),
      rank_by_col = dis_col,
      rank_dir = if (direction == "low_good") "low_good" else "high_good",
      tier_col = rank_tier_col, tier_labels = tl,
      cols = list(
        list(label = "With disability", value_col = dis_col, fmt = vf, emphasis = TRUE),
        list(label = "Without disability", value_col = nod_col, fmt = vf)),
      caption = paste0("States ranked by the ", tolower(value_label),
        " among people with disabilities; click a column heading to sort."),
      toggle_label = "Show the 5 lowest and 5 highest",
      restore_label = "Show all 51",
      compare_note = if (magnitude)
        "This measure has no better or worse direction; the Tier column orders states with a disability only by the size of the share. The map shades every state on one scale it shares with people without disabilities."
        else paste0("Tier and map colour answer different questions: the Tier column ranks each state only against other states with a disability, while the map shades every state on one scale it shares with people without disabilities. A state in the top tier here can still sit in a pale band on the map &mdash; that distance is the disability gap.")),
    footnotes = cfg$footnotes, pums_year = pums_year)
  build_dual_sheet(spec, data, acs_year)
}
```

# Community Living factsheets

Rebuilt on the simplified single-indicator template (2026-09-01). The two
Community Living sheets of three mapped indicators each are now **six sheets**,
one indicator apiece: Living in Community, Living at Home, Non-Institutional
Group Quarters (from the old *Living in Community*); Living in Institution,
Nursing Homes, Correctional Facilities (from the old *Living in Institution*).
Each follows the Mockup F grammar via the shared `build_dual_sheet()`.

Directions: community share and living at home are high-is-better; the three
institutional measures are low-is-better; non-institutional group quarters keeps
its **magnitude** framing (no better/worse claim) — its dual map, legend and
ranked-table chips read "Highest quarter" through "Lowest quarter".

Every map is a comparative PWD/PWOD pair on one scale pooled across disability
status, so a band names position on the shared rate scale rather than rank among
states. *Living in Community* and *Living in Institution* remain exact
complements (community % + institutional % = 100 on the common base).

```{r cl-build}
#| label: cl-build
# All six Community Living sheets go through the shared build_split_sheet().
# Row order of cl_national: 1 home | 2 GQ | 3 community | 4 inst | 5 nursing |
# 6 corrections | 7 other institutional.
build_cl_sheets <- function(cl, acs_year, content) {
  p1  <- function(x) fmt_pct(x, 1)
  N   <- cl_national
  ey  <- "ADA-PARC &middot; Community Living"
  src <- paste0("Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year ",
    "estimates (", acs_year - 4, "&ndash;", acs_year, ").")
  pop <- "People with a disability of any age, in every type of residence"

  kn <- function(natrow, unit, card3, fmt = p1)
    list(
      list(number = fmt(N$pwd[natrow]),
           label = paste0("of people with disabilities ", unit)),
      list(number = fmt(N$no_disability[natrow]),
           label = paste0("of people without disabilities ", unit)),
      card3)

  sheet <- function(id, out_file, title, subtitle, key, natrow,
                    dis_col, nod_col, ptd, ptn, rtc, direction,
                    brk, pop_detail, value_label, unit, card3, spot_labels,
                    magnitude = FALSE, vfmt = NULL) {
    vf <- vfmt %||% p1
    build_split_sheet(
      id, out_file, title, subtitle, key, cl,
      dis_col, nod_col, ptd, ptn, rtc, direction, brk,
      pop, pop_detail, value_label, paste0("of people with disabilities ", unit),
      kn(natrow, unit, card3, fmt = vf), spot_labels, acs_year, src,
      magnitude = magnitude, eyebrow = ey, value_fmt = vfmt)
  }

  c(
    # The two combined "Living in Community" / "Living in Institution" sheets
    # were retired September 2026 at the client's request; the granular
    # settings below (living at home, group quarters, nursing homes,
    # corrections) are what the site now carries. The pooled inputs and the
    # living_community / living_institution content blocks are left in place so
    # the aggregates can be reinstated by restoring these two sheet() calls.

    sheet("living-at-home", "factsheet-living-at-home.html",
      "Living at Home", "People With Disabilities Living in a House or Apartment, Not a Group Setting",
      "living_at_home", 1, "cl_home_dis", "cl_home_nodis",
      "ptier_home_dis", "ptier_home_nod", "tier_home", "high_good", cl_pooled$home,
      "Living at home is the largest component of the combined community-living rate.",
      "share living at home", "live at home",
      cp_pts_card(N$pwd[1], N$no_disability[1], "points lower for people with disabilities"),
      c("Highest share living at home", "Lowest share living at home")),

    sheet("group-quarters", "factsheet-group-quarters.html",
      "Non-Institutional Group Quarters", "People With Disabilities in Group Homes, Supported Living, Shelters or Dorms",
      "group_quarters", 2, "cl_nonintgq_dis", "cl_nonintgq_nodis",
      "ptier_gq_dis", "ptier_gq_nod", "tier_nonintgq", "high_good", cl_pooled$gq,
      "The category mixes group homes and supported living with shelters, transitional housing and college dormitories, so neither end of the range is a better outcome.",
      "share in non-institutional group quarters", "live in non-institutional group quarters",
      cp_pts_card(N$pwd[2], N$no_disability[2], "difference between the two populations, in points"),
      c("Largest share", "Smallest share"), magnitude = TRUE),

    sheet("nursing-homes", "factsheet-nursing-homes.html",
      "Nursing Homes", "People With Disabilities Living in a Nursing Home or Long-Term Medical Facility",
      "nursing_homes", 5, "cl_nursing_dis", "cl_nursing_nodis",
      "ptier_nursing_dis", "ptier_nursing_nod", "tier_nursing", "low_good", cl_pooled$nursing,
      "This is residents of all ages; age-specific rates use different denominators and are not shown here.",
      "nursing home rate", "live in a nursing home or medical facility",
      cp_pts_card(N$pwd[5], N$no_disability[5], "percentage points higher for people with disabilities"),
      c("Lowest nursing home rate", "Highest nursing home rate"),
      vfmt = fmt_pct_adaptive),

    sheet("corrections", "factsheet-corrections.html",
      "Correctional Facilities", "People With Disabilities Held in Prisons, Jails or Other Correctional Group Quarters",
      "corrections", 6, "cl_corrections_dis", "cl_corrections_nodis",
      "ptier_corr_dis", "ptier_corr_nod", "tier_corrections", "low_good", cl_pooled$corr,
      "Correctional facilities are the second largest institutional setting for people with disabilities.",
      "correctional confinement rate", "are held in a correctional facility",
      cp_ratio_card(N$pwd[6], N$no_disability[6], "as likely to be in a correctional facility with a disability"),
      c("Lowest correctional rate", "Highest correctional rate"))
  )
}

cl_paths <- build_cl_sheets(cl, acs_year, content)
cl_paths
```

# Poverty factsheet

Rebuilt 10 August 2026. The sheet was a single measure, ages 18 to 64, with
three summary-stat cards. It is now an **all-ages headline** with the three age
bands beneath it, and the cards are gone.

Two things had to be true before this was publishable. First, the three age
bands had to be computed the same way; until 10 August 2026 they were not, and
`docs/poverty-factsheet-plan.qmd` section 3 records what was wrong. Second, the
all-ages figure had to be exact rather than a weighted approximation, which it
is: C18130 partitions the population for whom poverty status is determined into
exactly these three age groups, so the all-ages rate is the sum of the three
numerators over the sum of the three denominators.

**Two scale regimes, and the split between them is deliberate.**

*The all-ages pair is one comparative map and shares one scale.* Breaks are
quartiles of the with-disability and without-disability series **pooled**, and a
single key sits under the pair. This is what `render_national_map()` does for
every `display_type == "comp"` indicator in the dashboard: it builds
`combined_var <- c(estimate, estimate_2)`, cuts both panels on those breaks and
draws one shared legend. Matching it here means a shade means the same rate on
both fact sheet panels and the same rate again on the national map of the same
indicator. The gap between the two panels *is* the disparity, read directly off
the colour rather than off two sets of legend numbers.

*The three age maps stay self-ranked, one scale each.* They are not a
comparative pair; they are three populations that differ in level for reasons
that have nothing to do with state performance. Pooling across them produced 38
Excellent and zero Poor on the 65-plus map and zero Excellent on the 18-64 map,
which says only that poverty falls after 65. Each of the three keeps
`fs_assign_tiers(x, "low_good")` with no `breaks` argument over the 51 states
and DC, Puerto Rico excluded so it cannot stretch a break, and each gets
13 / 12 / 13 / 13 states.

**The pooled pair does not carry Excellent and Poor.** On every other map those
words are claims about where a state sits **among states**. Pooled across
disability status they would become claims about which side of the national
disability gap a panel is on: zero Excellent and 24 Poor with disability,
26 Excellent and zero Poor without. The colour ramp is unchanged and still runs
dark = lower rate, but the shared key, the tooltips and the SVG descriptions on
this pair name the four bands by position on the scale rather than by
performance, so nothing asserts that 24 states are Poor at serving disabled
residents when what is showing is a national gap. `ADAPARC_TIER_LABEL_BAND_LOW`
in `assets/adaparc-map.js` holds those labels; the age maps are untouched and
still read Excellent through Poor.

The cost on the age maps is real and is handled rather than hidden. Excellent on
the 65-plus map is not the same rate as Excellent on the 18-64 map, so every
legend prints its own numeric range on all four chips, and the captions say the
scales differ.

Direction is `low_good` throughout. A with-disability rate above 25% is flagged
in the all-ages table, and the flag carries a visually hidden text label so it
is not conveyed by colour alone.

**The introduction quotes no typed numbers.** Every figure in the prose arrives
as a `{token}` filled from `pov_values` at render time, and
`fs_assert_no_tokens()` stops the build if one fails to resolve. Employment and
Education still type theirs; they should be migrated next.

Variables: `pct_cni_allages_poverty_dis` / `_nodis`, and the `under18`, `18to64`
and `65plus` equivalents, with their `pop_cni_*_poverty_*` counts.

```{r poverty-data}
#| label: poverty-data
pr_row <- national |> filter(ABBR == "PR")
us_row <- national |> filter(ABBR == "USA")

pv <- states_df |>
  transmute(
    fips, ABBR, name = NAME,
    all_dis   = pct_cni_allages_poverty_dis,
    all_nod   = pct_cni_allages_poverty_nodis,
    u18_dis   = pct_cni_under18_poverty_dis,
    u18_nod   = pct_cni_under18_poverty_nodis,
    a1864_dis = pct_cni_18to64_poverty_dis,
    a1864_nod = pct_cni_18to64_poverty_nodis,
    a65_dis   = pct_cni_65plus_poverty_dis,
    a65_nod   = pct_cni_65plus_poverty_nodis,
    n_all_dis = pop_cni_allages_poverty_dis,
    n_u18_dis = pop_cni_under18_poverty_dis,
    n_1864_dis = pop_cni_18to64_poverty_dis,
    n_65_dis  = pop_cni_65plus_poverty_dis
  )

# The partition is the whole basis of the all-ages figure, so it is asserted
# here as well as in the pipeline. This repository reads a copied Rds; a guard
# that only runs in the repository that wrote the file does not protect the
# sheet that reads it.
stopifnot(
  "all-ages poverty count must equal the sum of the three age bands" =
    all(abs((pv$n_u18_dis + pv$n_1864_dis + pv$n_65_dis) - pv$n_all_dis) < 1e-6)
)

# The all-ages pair is this sheet's one comparative map, so it shares a scale
# across disability status the way the dashboard's comp indicators do: quartiles
# of the two series pooled, both panels cut on those breaks, one key. Puerto
# Rico stays out of the pooled vector for the same reason it stays off the maps,
# at roughly 47 percent all ages it would stretch the top break on its own.
pov_all_breaks <- fs_tier_breaks(c(pv$all_dis, pv$all_nod))

# The three age maps are not a comparative pair and keep the house standard, one
# self-ranked scale each. No `breaks` argument, so fs_assign_tiers computes its
# own from the series it is tiering.
pv <- pv |>
  mutate(
    tier_all_dis = fs_assign_tiers(all_dis, "low_good", breaks = pov_all_breaks),
    tier_all_nod = fs_assign_tiers(all_nod, "low_good", breaks = pov_all_breaks),
    tier_u18     = fs_assign_tiers(u18_dis,   "low_good"),
    tier_1864    = fs_assign_tiers(a1864_dis, "low_good"),
    tier_65      = fs_assign_tiers(a65_dis,   "low_good")
  )

# ---- pooled PWD/PWOD tiers for the simplified template (2026-09-01) ----------
# The rebuilt sheet shows every band, all ages and the three age groups, as a
# comparative dual map on ONE scale pooled across disability status, matching
# the all-ages pair the sheet already used. Each age band pools only within
# itself (poverty differs by age for reasons unrelated to state performance),
# so the four bins still describe position on that band's shared rate scale.
# Labels stay Excellent-to-Poor (client decision); PR is kept out of every
# pooled vector, as it is out of the maps.
pov_pooled <- list(
  all   = pov_all_breaks,
  u18   = fs_tier_breaks(c(pv$u18_dis,   pv$u18_nod)),
  a1864 = fs_tier_breaks(c(pv$a1864_dis, pv$a1864_nod)),
  a65   = fs_tier_breaks(c(pv$a65_dis,   pv$a65_nod))
)
pv <- pv |>
  mutate(
    ptier_u18_dis   = fs_assign_tiers(u18_dis,   "low_good", breaks = pov_pooled$u18),
    ptier_u18_nod   = fs_assign_tiers(u18_nod,   "low_good", breaks = pov_pooled$u18),
    ptier_1864_dis  = fs_assign_tiers(a1864_dis, "low_good", breaks = pov_pooled$a1864),
    ptier_1864_nod  = fs_assign_tiers(a1864_nod, "low_good", breaks = pov_pooled$a1864),
    ptier_65_dis    = fs_assign_tiers(a65_dis,   "low_good", breaks = pov_pooled$a65),
    ptier_65_nod    = fs_assign_tiers(a65_nod,   "low_good", breaks = pov_pooled$a65),
    # self-ranked among the 51 with-disability jurisdictions, for the ranked-
    # table Tier column (the all-ages map keeps the pooled scale)
    tier_all_sr     = fs_assign_tiers(all_dis, "low_good")
  )

# Breaks kept for the legends. One entry for the shared all-ages scale, because
# there is now one key for the pair, and one per age map. Recomputing here with
# the same function on the same vector is the only way to label a chip with the
# range it actually represents.
pov_breaks <- list(
  all_shared = pov_all_breaks,
  u18        = fs_tier_breaks(pv$u18_dis),
  a1864      = fs_tier_breaks(pv$a1864_dis),
  a65        = fs_tier_breaks(pv$a65_dis)
)

# Equal-count quartiles over 51 jurisdictions must land 13/12/13/13 on each of
# the three self-ranked age maps. A lopsided count there means a tie has
# collapsed a break and the tier labels stop meaning what they say.
tier_counts <- vapply(
  c("tier_u18", "tier_1864", "tier_65"),
  function(col) as.integer(table(factor(pv[[col]],
    levels = c("excellent", "above", "below", "poor")))),
  integer(4))
stopifnot(
  "every self-ranked poverty age map must be an equal-count quartile split" =
    all(abs(tier_counts - nrow(pv) / 4) <= 1)
)

# The pooled pair is deliberately lopsided panel by panel, that asymmetry is the
# disparity. What must still hold is that the two panels together are an
# equal-count split of the pooled vector, which is what makes the shared key's
# printed ranges true of both.
band_counts <- vapply(
  c("tier_all_dis", "tier_all_nod"),
  function(col) as.integer(table(factor(pv[[col]],
    levels = c("excellent", "above", "below", "poor")))),
  integer(4))
# Slack of 2 rather than 1: the pooled vector is 102 values, so a tie sitting on
# a break moves more states than it can on a 51-value map.
stopifnot(
  "the pooled all-ages pair must be an equal-count split across both panels" =
    all(abs(rowSums(band_counts) - nrow(pv) / 2) <= 2)
)

list(age_maps = tier_counts, all_ages_pooled = band_counts)
```

```{r poverty-national}
#| label: poverty-national
# National figures, and the values the introduction and the section leads quote.
#
# Nothing here is typed into docs/factsheet-prose.docx. The prose carries tokens
# and this chunk fills them, so the sentences track the vintage instead of
# needing to be checked against it. If a token is misspelled in the document,
# fs_assert_no_tokens() stops the render rather than publishing a stray brace.
pov_national <- tibble::tibble(
  group = c("All ages", "Under 18", "18 to 64", "65 and over"),
  pwd = c(us_row$pct_cni_allages_poverty_dis,
          us_row$pct_cni_under18_poverty_dis,
          us_row$pct_cni_18to64_poverty_dis,
          us_row$pct_cni_65plus_poverty_dis),
  no_disability = c(us_row$pct_cni_allages_poverty_nodis,
                    us_row$pct_cni_under18_poverty_nodis,
                    us_row$pct_cni_18to64_poverty_nodis,
                    us_row$pct_cni_65plus_poverty_nodis)
) |>
  mutate(ratio = pwd / no_disability)

# Bare numbers, because the prose supplies the word "percent" itself. A
# formatter that emitted "20.4%" would read as "20.4% percent" in the sentence.
num1 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1)

pov_values <- c(
  pov_dis_all    = num1(us_row$pct_cni_allages_poverty_dis),
  pov_nod_all    = num1(us_row$pct_cni_allages_poverty_nodis),
  pov_ratio_1864 = num1(us_row$pct_cni_18to64_poverty_dis /
                        us_row$pct_cni_18to64_poverty_nodis),
  pov_count_dis  = paste0(num1(us_row$pop_cni_allages_poverty_dis / 1e6),
                          " million"),
  # The composition framing the removed NCD sentence was reaching for, computed
  # from our own data. People with disabilities are a modest share of the
  # population and a larger share of the people below the line.
  pov_share_of_pop = num1(
    us_row$pop_cni_allages_povbase_dis /
      (us_row$pop_cni_allages_povbase_dis + us_row$pop_cni_allages_povbase_nodis) * 100),
  pov_share_of_poor = num1(
    us_row$pop_cni_allages_poverty_dis /
      (us_row$pop_cni_allages_poverty_dis + us_row$pop_cni_allages_poverty_nodis) * 100)
)

pov_national |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2)))
pov_values
```

```{r poverty-build}
#| label: poverty-build
# Rebuilt on the simplified single-indicator template (2026-09-01). The all-ages
# pair is the full-treatment lead (takeaway, dual pooled map, Why This Matters
# with Key Numbers and a best/worst spotlight, explainer, ranked table). The
# three age bands follow as light sections: a comparative dual map on their own
# pooled scale plus a ranked table, no Why This Matters furniture. Every map is
# a PWD/PWOD pair; Puerto Rico stays off the maps, the pooled scales and the
# ranked tables, with its rate noted in the captions.
build_poverty <- function(pv, pr_row, acs_year, cfg, values) {
  pct1 <- function(x) fmt_pct(x, 1)
  fill <- function(x) fs_assert_no_tokens(
    fs_fill_values(fs_fill_years(unlist(x), acs_year = acs_year), values), "poverty")

  src <- paste0("Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year ",
                "estimates (", acs_year - 4, "&ndash;", acs_year, "), Table C18130.")
  read_shared <- paste0(
    "Both maps use one colour scale, so a shade means the same poverty rate on ",
    "either map, and the difference between them is the disability gap read ",
    "straight off the colour. The four bands are cut on the two populations ",
    "pooled. Hover or tab through either map for a state's exact rate. ")

  o  <- order(pv$all_dis)
  bw <- list(best = pv[o[1], ], worst = pv[o[nrow(pv)], ])
  ratio_all <- pov_national$ratio[1]

  # ---- three light age-band sections -------------------------------------------
  age_band <- function(id, band_title, dis_col, nod_col, td, tn, rtc, brk, pr_val,
                       lead) {
    map_spec <- list(
      id = id, map_title = paste0(band_title, ": People With and Without Disabilities"),
      dis_col = dis_col, nod_col = nod_col,
      tier_dis_col = td, tier_nod_col = tn,
      direction = "low_good", fmt = pct1,
      value_label = "Poverty rate", pooled_breaks = brk,
      legend_best = "lowest rate", legend_worst = "highest rate",
      svg_title_dis = paste0(band_title, ": people with disabilities, by U.S. state"),
      svg_desc_dis = paste0("Choropleth of the 50 states and DC shaded by the ",
        "share of people with disabilities in this age group living below the ",
        "poverty line, on a scale shared with the map for people without ",
        "disabilities. Darker is a lower rate. Full data is in the table below."),
      svg_title_nod = paste0(band_title, ": people without disabilities, by U.S. state"),
      svg_desc_nod = paste0("Choropleth of the 50 states and DC on the same ",
        "shared scale for people without disabilities in this age group. Full ",
        "data is in the table below."),
      caption = paste0(read_shared, "Darker maroon marks a lower poverty rate. ",
        "Puerto Rico (", fmt_pct(pr_val, 1), ") is not shown. ", src))
    ranked_spec <- list(
      id = id, section_heading = paste0(band_title, ", by State"),
      intro = paste0("Every state and DC, ranked by the poverty rate among ",
        "people with disabilities in this age group. The two maps above are ",
        "shaded on one scale pooled with people without disabilities; the Tier ",
        "column here ranks each state among states with a disability."),
      rank_by_col = dis_col, rank_dir = "low_good", tier_col = rtc,
      cols = list(
        list(label = "With disability", value_col = dis_col, fmt = pct1, emphasis = TRUE),
        list(label = "Without disability", value_col = nod_col, fmt = pct1)),
      caption = paste0("States ranked by the poverty rate among people with ",
        "disabilities in this age group; click a column heading to sort."),
      toggle_label = "Show the 5 lowest and 5 highest",
      restore_label = "Show all 51",
      compare_note = paste0("Tier and map colour answer different questions: the ",
        "Tier column ranks each state only against other states with a disability, ",
        "while the maps shade every state on one scale shared with people without ",
        "disabilities, so a top-tier state can still sit in a pale band. Each age ",
        "band ranks its own with-disability jurisdictions, so a tier here is not ",
        "the same rate as the tier of the same name in another band."))
    fs_light_dual(map_spec, ranked_spec, pv, lead = fill(lead))
  }

  bands <- list(
    age_band("pov-under18", "Poverty Rate, Children Under 18",
             "u18_dis", "u18_nod", "ptier_u18_dis", "ptier_u18_nod", "tier_u18",
             pov_pooled$u18, pr_row$pct_cni_under18_poverty_dis, cfg$under18_lead),
    age_band("pov-1864", "Poverty Rate, Working-Age Adults 18 to 64",
             "a1864_dis", "a1864_nod", "ptier_1864_dis", "ptier_1864_nod", "tier_1864",
             pov_pooled$a1864, pr_row$pct_cni_18to64_poverty_dis, cfg$age1864_lead),
    age_band("pov-65plus", "Poverty Rate, Adults 65 and Over",
             "a65_dis", "a65_nod", "ptier_65_dis", "ptier_65_nod", "tier_65",
             pov_pooled$a65, pr_row$pct_cni_65plus_poverty_dis, cfg$age65plus_lead)
  )

  tail_html <- paste0(
    '    <h2 class="section-heading">Poverty by Age</h2>\n',
    '    <p class="section-intro">The headline above covers all ages together. ',
    'Poverty falls sharply after 65, because Social Security and Medicare reach ',
    'almost everyone, so each age band below is drawn on its own scale pooled ',
    'across disability status. Read the ranges on each key before comparing one ',
    'band with another.</p>\n\n',
    paste(vapply(bands, `[[`, character(1), "html"), collapse = "\n"))
  tail_js <- paste(vapply(bands, `[[`, character(1), "js"), collapse = "\n\n")

  # ---- the all-ages lead -----------------------------------------------------
  spec <- list(
    id = "poverty", out_file = "factsheet-poverty.html",
    page_title = "Poverty | ADA-PARC Fact Sheet",
    page_desc = paste0("ADA-PARC fact sheet on poverty among people with ",
      "disabilities, all ages and by age group, with state-by-state data."),
    header_title = "Poverty", header_eyebrow = "ADA-PARC &middot; Work &amp; Economic",
    header_subtitle = "People With Disabilities Living Below the Poverty Line",
    population_note = list(
      note = "People of all ages for whom poverty status is determined",
      detail = paste0("The Census Bureau does not assess poverty status for ",
        "everyone. People in group quarters &mdash; including nursing homes, ",
        "correctional facilities and college dormitories &mdash; and unrelated ",
        "individuals under 15 are outside every figure on this sheet.")),
    takeaway = fill(cfg$takeaway),
    why_matters = fill(cfg$intro),
    key_numbers = list(
      list(number = fmt_pct(pov_national$pwd[1], 1),
           label = "of people with disabilities live below the poverty line"),
      list(number = fmt_pct(pov_national$no_disability[1], 1),
           label = "of people without disabilities live below the poverty line"),
      list(number = paste0(formatC(ratio_all, format = "f", digits = 1), "&times;"),
           label = "as likely to be in poverty with a disability", gap = TRUE)),
    spotlight = list(
      best = list(label = "Lowest poverty rate", state = bw$best$name,
        value = paste0(pct1(bw$best$all_dis),
          " of people with disabilities live below the poverty line"),
        note = paste0("Against ", pct1(bw$best$all_nod),
          " of people without disabilities in the same state.")),
      worst = list(label = "Highest poverty rate", state = bw$worst$name,
        value = paste0(pct1(bw$worst$all_dis),
          " of people with disabilities live below the poverty line"),
        note = paste0("Against ", pct1(bw$worst$all_nod),
          " of people without disabilities in the same state."))),
    explainer_heading = "What This Map Measures",
    explainer = fill(cfg$allages_lead),
    map = list(
      id = "poverty", map_title = "Poverty Rate, All Ages, People With and Without Disabilities",
      dis_col = "all_dis", nod_col = "all_nod",
      tier_dis_col = "tier_all_dis", tier_nod_col = "tier_all_nod",
      direction = "low_good", fmt = pct1, value_label = "Poverty rate",
      pooled_breaks = pov_pooled$all,
      legend_best = "lowest rate", legend_worst = "highest rate",
      svg_title_dis = "Poverty rate among people with disabilities of all ages, by U.S. state",
      svg_desc_dis = paste0("Choropleth of the 50 states and DC shaded by the ",
        "share of people with disabilities of any age living below the poverty ",
        "line, on a scale shared with the map for people without disabilities. ",
        "Darker is a lower rate. Full data is in the table below."),
      svg_title_nod = "Poverty rate among people without disabilities of all ages, by U.S. state",
      svg_desc_nod = paste0("Choropleth of the 50 states and DC on the same ",
        "shared scale for people without disabilities, so this map is broadly ",
        "darker. Full data is in the table below."),
      caption = paste0(read_shared, "Darker maroon marks a lower poverty rate. ",
        "Puerto Rico (with disability ", fmt_pct(pr_row$pct_cni_allages_poverty_dis, 1),
        ") is not shown. ", src)),
    ranked = list(
      id = "poverty", section_heading = "Poverty Rate, All Ages, by State",
      intro = paste0("Every state and DC, ranked by the poverty rate among ",
        "people with disabilities of any age. The maps above are shaded on one ",
        "scale pooled with people without disabilities; the Tier column here ",
        "ranks each state among states with a disability. Search, sort, or ",
        "narrow to the five lowest and five highest."),
      rank_by_col = "all_dis", rank_dir = "low_good", tier_col = "tier_all_sr",
      cols = list(
        list(label = "With disability", value_col = "all_dis", fmt = pct1, emphasis = TRUE),
        list(label = "Without disability", value_col = "all_nod", fmt = pct1)),
      caption = "States ranked by the poverty rate among people with disabilities of all ages; click a column heading to sort.",
      toggle_label = "Show the 5 lowest and 5 highest",
      restore_label = "Show all 51",
      compare_note = paste0("Tier and map colour answer different questions: the ",
        "Tier column ranks each state only against other states with a disability, ",
        "while the map shades every state on one scale it shares with people ",
        "without disabilities. A state in the top tier here can still sit in a ",
        "pale band on the map &mdash; that distance is the disability gap. Showing ",
        "all 50 states and DC by default. Puerto Rico is not ranked here; its ",
        "rates are in the map captions.")),
    footnotes = cfg$footnotes,
    tail_html = tail_html, tail_js = tail_js)

  build_dual_sheet(spec, pv, acs_year)
}

poverty_path <- build_poverty(pv, pr_row, acs_year, content$poverty, pov_values)
poverty_path
```

# Employment factsheets

Rebuilt on the simplified single-indicator template (2026-09-01). The one
Employment sheet of three mapped C18120 categories is now **three sheets** &mdash;
Employment, Not in the Labor Force, Unemployment &mdash; one indicator each,
following the Mockup F grammar: takeaway, a comparative PWD/PWOD dual map on one
pooled scale, Why This Matters with Key Numbers and a best/worst spotlight, an
explainer, and a searchable ranked table. `build_employment_sheets()` assembles
all three through the shared `build_dual_sheet()`.

Directions: employed is high-is-better; unemployed and not-in-labor-force are
both low-is-better. The not-in-labor-force direction is a deliberate editorial
choice rather than a property of the data, kept with the caveat stated in the
explainer prose (client decision, 2026-09-01).

Each map's four bands are cut on the with-disability and without-disability
series **pooled**, so a band names position on the shared rate scale rather than
rank among states: the best state for disabled employment still lands in a
middle band, and that gap is the finding.

These figures were independently reconciled against a fresh Census API pull of
C18120 in July 2026 with zero discrepancies across all national, state and place
records; see `scripts/audit_employment_acs.R` and
`docs/employment_audit_2026-07-28.html`. `fs_emp_measures()` re-checks the same
properties at build time.

```{r emp-data}
#| label: emp-data
emp <- states_df |>
  fs_emp_measures() |>
  mutate(
    name = NAME,
    tier_employed   = fs_assign_tiers(emp_employed_dis,   "high_good"),
    tier_unemployed = fs_assign_tiers(emp_unemployed_dis, "low_good"),
    tier_notlabor   = fs_assign_tiers(emp_notlabor_dis,   "low_good")
  )

# ---- pooled PWD/PWOD tiers for the simplified template's dual maps -----------
# Each of the three split sheets shows a comparative dual map on ONE scale
# pooled across disability status, the way the dashboard's `comp` indicators and
# the poverty all-ages pair already do. The four bins therefore describe where a
# state sits on the shared rate scale, not among states; the best state for PWD
# employment still lands in a middle band, and that gap is the point. Labels
# stay Excellent-to-Poor (client decision, 2026-09-01).
emp_pooled <- list(
  employed   = fs_tier_breaks(c(emp$emp_employed_dis,   emp$emp_employed_nodis)),
  unemployed = fs_tier_breaks(c(emp$emp_unemployed_dis, emp$emp_unemployed_nodis)),
  notlabor   = fs_tier_breaks(c(emp$emp_notlabor_dis,   emp$emp_notlabor_nodis))
)
emp <- emp |>
  mutate(
    ptier_employed_dis   = fs_assign_tiers(emp_employed_dis,   "high_good", breaks = emp_pooled$employed),
    ptier_employed_nod   = fs_assign_tiers(emp_employed_nodis,  "high_good", breaks = emp_pooled$employed),
    ptier_unemployed_dis = fs_assign_tiers(emp_unemployed_dis,  "low_good",  breaks = emp_pooled$unemployed),
    ptier_unemployed_nod = fs_assign_tiers(emp_unemployed_nodis,"low_good",  breaks = emp_pooled$unemployed),
    ptier_notlabor_dis   = fs_assign_tiers(emp_notlabor_dis,    "low_good",  breaks = emp_pooled$notlabor),
    ptier_notlabor_nod   = fs_assign_tiers(emp_notlabor_nodis,  "low_good",  breaks = emp_pooled$notlabor)
  )

# Population-weighted national shares. The introduction in
# docs/factsheet-prose.docx quotes 43 percent, 78 percent, 10.9 percent and
# 4.8 percent as typed text; check them against this table when the vintage moves.
emp_national <- tibble::tibble(
  measure = c("Employed", "Unemployed", "Not in labor force",
              "In the labor force", "Unemployment rate (of labor force)"),
  pwd = c(
    sum(emp$pop_cni_18to64_employed_dis),
    sum(emp$pop_cni_18to64_unemployed_dis),
    sum(emp$pop_cni_18to64_notlabor_dis),
    sum(emp$pop_cni_18to64_employed_dis) + sum(emp$pop_cni_18to64_unemployed_dis),
    NA) / sum(emp$emp_base_dis) * 100,
  no_disability = c(
    sum(emp$pop_cni_18to64_employed_nodis),
    sum(emp$pop_cni_18to64_unemployed_nodis),
    sum(emp$pop_cni_18to64_notlabor_nodis),
    sum(emp$pop_cni_18to64_employed_nodis) + sum(emp$pop_cni_18to64_unemployed_nodis),
    NA) / sum(emp$emp_base_nodis) * 100)

# The unemployment rate has its own denominator, so it is filled in separately.
emp_national$pwd[5] <- sum(emp$pop_cni_18to64_unemployed_dis) /
  (sum(emp$pop_cni_18to64_employed_dis) + sum(emp$pop_cni_18to64_unemployed_dis)) * 100
emp_national$no_disability[5] <- sum(emp$pop_cni_18to64_unemployed_nodis) /
  (sum(emp$pop_cni_18to64_employed_nodis) + sum(emp$pop_cni_18to64_unemployed_nodis)) * 100

emp_national |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

```{r emp-build}
#| label: emp-build
build_employment_sheets <- function(emp, acs_year, content) {
  pct1 <- function(x) fmt_pct(x, 1)
  pct0 <- function(x) fmt_pct(x, 0)
  N    <- emp_national   # emp-data: rows Employed / Unemployed / NILF / InLF / Urate
  xN   <- function(i, g) if (g == "dis") N$pwd[i] else N$no_disability[i]

  eyebrow    <- "ADA-PARC &middot; Work &amp; Economic"
  src_c18120 <- paste0("Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey ",
                       "5-year estimates (", acs_year - 4, "&ndash;", acs_year,
                       "), Table C18120.")
  read_shared <- paste0(
    "Both maps use one colour scale, so a shade means the same rate on either ",
    "map. The four bands are cut on the two populations pooled, which is why ",
    "the map for people with disabilities sits in the lighter bands and the ",
    "one for people without disabilities in the darker ones — that distance ",
    "is the disability gap. Hover or tab through either map for a state's exact ",
    "figure. ")

  bw_of <- function(vcol, dir) {
    o <- if (dir == "high_good") order(-emp[[vcol]]) else order(emp[[vcol]])
    list(best = emp[o[1], ], worst = emp[o[nrow(emp)], ])
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- Employment
  bw <- bw_of("emp_employed_dis", "high_good")
  employment <- list(
    id = "employment", out_file = "factsheet-employment.html",
    page_title = "Employment | ADA-PARC Fact Sheet",
    page_desc = paste0("ADA-PARC fact sheet on the share of working-age people ",
      "with disabilities who are employed, with state-by-state data."),
    header_title = "Employment", header_eyebrow = eyebrow,
    header_subtitle = "Working-Age People With Disabilities Who Hold a Job",
    population_note = list(
      note = "The civilian noninstitutionalized population ages 18 to 64",
      detail = paste0("People living in nursing homes, other institutions and ",
        "correctional facilities are outside this universe, as is anyone on ",
        "active military duty.")),
    takeaway = content$employment$takeaway,
    why_matters = content$employment$intro,
    key_numbers = list(
      list(number = pct0(N$pwd[1]),
           label = "of working-age people with disabilities are employed"),
      list(number = pct0(N$pwd[4]),
           label = "are in the labor force &mdash; working or looking for work"),
      list(number = paste0(formatC(N$no_disability[1] / N$pwd[1],
                                   format = "f", digits = 1), "&times;"),
           label = "as likely to be employed without a disability", gap = TRUE)),
    spotlight = list(
      best = list(label = "Highest employment rate", state = bw$best$name,
        value = paste0(pct1(bw$best$emp_employed_dis),
          " of working-age people with disabilities are employed"),
        note = paste0("Still below the same state's rate for people without ",
          "disabilities (", pct1(bw$best$emp_employed_nodis), ").")),
      worst = list(label = "Lowest employment rate", state = bw$worst$name,
        value = paste0(pct1(bw$worst$emp_employed_dis),
          " of working-age people with disabilities are employed"),
        note = paste0("Against ", pct1(bw$worst$emp_employed_nodis),
          " of people without disabilities in the same state."))),
    explainer_heading = "What This Map Measures",
    explainer = content$employment$employed_lead,
    map = list(
      id = "employment",
      map_title = "Employment Rate, People With and Without Disabilities",
      dis_col = "emp_employed_dis", nod_col = "emp_employed_nodis",
      tier_dis_col = "ptier_employed_dis", tier_nod_col = "ptier_employed_nod",
      direction = "high_good", fmt = pct1, value_label = "Employment rate",
      pooled_breaks = emp_pooled$employed,
      legend_best = "highest rate", legend_worst = "lowest rate",
      svg_title_dis = "Employment rate among working-age people with disabilities, by U.S. state",
      svg_desc_dis = paste0("Choropleth of the 50 states and DC shaded by the ",
        "share of working-age people with disabilities who are employed, on a ",
        "scale shared with the map for people without disabilities. Darker is a ",
        "higher rate. Full data is in the table below."),
      svg_title_nod = "Employment rate among working-age people without disabilities, by U.S. state",
      svg_desc_nod = paste0("Choropleth of the 50 states and DC on the same ",
        "shared scale for people without disabilities, so this map is broadly ",
        "darker. Full data is in the table below."),
      caption = paste0(read_shared, "Darker maroon marks a higher employment ",
        "rate. ", src_c18120)),
    ranked = list(
      id = "employment", section_heading = "Employment Rate, by State",
      intro = paste0("Every state and DC, ranked by the employment rate among ",
        "working-age people with disabilities. The maps above are shaded on one ",
        "scale pooled with people without disabilities; the Tier column here ",
        "ranks each state among states with a disability. Search, sort, or narrow ",
        "to the five lowest and five highest."),
      rank_by_col = "emp_employed_dis", rank_dir = "high_good",
      tier_col = "tier_employed",   # self-ranked among states with a disability
      cols = list(
        list(label = "With disability", value_col = "emp_employed_dis",
             fmt = pct1, emphasis = TRUE),
        list(label = "Without disability", value_col = "emp_employed_nodis",
             fmt = pct1)),
      caption = "States ranked by the employment rate among working-age people with disabilities; click a column heading to sort.",
      toggle_label = "Show the 5 lowest and 5 highest",
      restore_label = "Show all 51",
      compare_note = paste0("Tier and map colour answer different questions: the Tier column ranks each state only against other states with a disability, while the map shades every state on one scale it shares with people without disabilities. A state in the top tier here can still sit in a pale band on the map &mdash; that distance is the disability gap. Showing all 50 states and DC by default.")),
    footnotes = content$employment$footnotes)

  # -------------------------------------------------------- Not in Labor Force
  bw <- bw_of("emp_notlabor_dis", "low_good")
  nilf <- list(
    id = "not-in-labor-force", out_file = "factsheet-not-in-labor-force.html",
    page_title = "Not in the Labor Force | ADA-PARC Fact Sheet",
    page_desc = paste0("ADA-PARC fact sheet on the share of working-age people ",
      "with disabilities who are neither working nor looking for work."),
    header_title = "Not in the Labor Force", header_eyebrow = eyebrow,
    header_subtitle = "Working-Age People With Disabilities Neither Working Nor Looking for Work",
    population_note = list(
      note = "The civilian noninstitutionalized population ages 18 to 64",
      detail = paste0("People in institutions and correctional facilities, and ",
        "anyone on active military duty, are outside this universe.")),
    takeaway = content$not_in_labor_force$takeaway,
    why_matters = content$not_in_labor_force$intro,
    key_numbers = list(
      list(number = pct0(N$pwd[3]),
           label = "of working-age people with disabilities are not in the labor force"),
      list(number = pct0(N$no_disability[3]),
           label = "of working-age people without disabilities are not in the labor force"),
      list(number = paste0(formatC(N$pwd[3] / N$no_disability[3],
                                   format = "f", digits = 1), "&times;"),
           label = "as likely to be outside the labor force with a disability", gap = TRUE)),
    spotlight = list(
      best = list(label = "Lowest share out of the labor force", state = bw$best$name,
        value = paste0(pct1(bw$best$emp_notlabor_dis),
          " of working-age people with disabilities are not in the labor force"),
        note = paste0("Against ", pct1(bw$best$emp_notlabor_nodis),
          " of people without disabilities in the same state.")),
      worst = list(label = "Highest share out of the labor force", state = bw$worst$name,
        value = paste0(pct1(bw$worst$emp_notlabor_dis),
          " of working-age people with disabilities are not in the labor force"),
        note = paste0("Against ", pct1(bw$worst$emp_notlabor_nodis),
          " of people without disabilities in the same state."))),
    explainer_heading = "What This Map Measures",
    explainer = content$not_in_labor_force$notlabor_lead,
    map = list(
      id = "not-in-labor-force",
      map_title = "Share Not in the Labor Force, People With and Without Disabilities",
      dis_col = "emp_notlabor_dis", nod_col = "emp_notlabor_nodis",
      tier_dis_col = "ptier_notlabor_dis", tier_nod_col = "ptier_notlabor_nod",
      direction = "low_good", fmt = pct1,
      value_label = "Share not in the labor force",
      pooled_breaks = emp_pooled$notlabor,
      legend_best = "lowest rate", legend_worst = "highest rate",
      svg_title_dis = "Share of working-age people with disabilities not in the labor force, by U.S. state",
      svg_desc_dis = paste0("Choropleth of the 50 states and DC shaded by the ",
        "share of working-age people with disabilities who are neither working ",
        "nor looking for work, on a scale shared with the map for people ",
        "without disabilities. Darker is a lower share. Full data is in the ",
        "table below."),
      svg_title_nod = "Share of working-age people without disabilities not in the labor force, by U.S. state",
      svg_desc_nod = paste0("Choropleth of the 50 states and DC on the same ",
        "shared scale for people without disabilities, so this map is broadly ",
        "darker. Full data is in the table below."),
      caption = paste0(read_shared, "Darker maroon marks a lower share out of ",
        "the labor force; lower is treated as the more favourable outcome, ",
        "though the category also counts students, carers and people retired ",
        "before 65. ", src_c18120)),
    ranked = list(
      id = "not-in-labor-force",
      section_heading = "Share Not in the Labor Force, by State",
      intro = paste0("Every state and DC, ranked by the share of working-age ",
        "people with disabilities who are neither working nor looking for work. ",
        "The maps above use the pooled scale; the Tier column ranks each state ",
        "among states with a disability."),
      rank_by_col = "emp_notlabor_dis", rank_dir = "low_good",
      tier_col = "tier_notlabor",   # self-ranked among states with a disability
      cols = list(
        list(label = "With disability", value_col = "emp_notlabor_dis",
             fmt = pct1, emphasis = TRUE),
        list(label = "Without disability", value_col = "emp_notlabor_nodis",
             fmt = pct1)),
      caption = "States ranked by the share of working-age people with disabilities not in the labor force; click a column heading to sort.",
      toggle_label = "Show the 5 lowest and 5 highest",
      restore_label = "Show all 51",
      compare_note = paste0("Tier and map colour answer different questions: the Tier column ranks each state only against other states with a disability, while the map shades every state on one scale it shares with people without disabilities. A state in the top tier here can still sit in a pale band on the map &mdash; that distance is the disability gap. Showing all 50 states and DC by default.")),
    footnotes = content$not_in_labor_force$footnotes)

  # -------------------------------------------------------------- Unemployment
  bw <- bw_of("emp_unemployed_dis", "low_good")
  unemployment <- list(
    id = "unemployment", out_file = "factsheet-unemployment.html",
    page_title = "Unemployment | ADA-PARC Fact Sheet",
    page_desc = paste0("ADA-PARC fact sheet on unemployment among working-age ",
      "people with disabilities, with state-by-state data."),
    header_title = "Unemployment", header_eyebrow = eyebrow,
    header_subtitle = "Working-Age People With Disabilities Looking for Work",
    population_note = list(
      note = "The civilian noninstitutionalized population ages 18 to 64",
      detail = paste0("The mapped figure is a share of everyone in the age ",
        "group. The narrower unemployment rate — a share of the labor force ",
        "only — is in the table.")),
    takeaway = content$unemployment$takeaway,
    why_matters = content$unemployment$intro,
    key_numbers = list(
      list(number = fmt_pct(N$pwd[2], 1),
           label = "of all working-age people with disabilities are unemployed and looking for work"),
      list(number = fmt_pct(N$pwd[5], 1),
           label = "unemployment rate among those in the labor force"),
      list(number = paste0(formatC(N$pwd[5] / N$no_disability[5],
                                   format = "f", digits = 1), "&times;"),
           label = "the unemployment rate for people without a disability", gap = TRUE)),
    spotlight = list(
      best = list(label = "Lowest share unemployed", state = bw$best$name,
        value = paste0(fmt_pct(bw$best$emp_unemployed_dis, 1),
          " of working-age people with disabilities are unemployed"),
        note = paste0("Against ", fmt_pct(bw$best$emp_unemployed_nodis, 1),
          " of people without disabilities in the same state.")),
      worst = list(label = "Highest share unemployed", state = bw$worst$name,
        value = paste0(fmt_pct(bw$worst$emp_unemployed_dis, 1),
          " of working-age people with disabilities are unemployed"),
        note = paste0("Against ", fmt_pct(bw$worst$emp_unemployed_nodis, 1),
          " of people without disabilities in the same state."))),
    explainer_heading = "What This Map Measures",
    explainer = content$unemployment$unemployed_lead,
    map = list(
      id = "unemployment",
      map_title = "Share Unemployed, People With and Without Disabilities",
      dis_col = "emp_unemployed_dis", nod_col = "emp_unemployed_nodis",
      tier_dis_col = "ptier_unemployed_dis", tier_nod_col = "ptier_unemployed_nod",
      direction = "low_good", fmt = function(x) fmt_pct(x, 1),
      value_label = "Share unemployed",
      pooled_breaks = emp_pooled$unemployed, range_digits = 1,
      legend_best = "lowest rate", legend_worst = "highest rate",
      svg_title_dis = "Share of working-age people with disabilities who are unemployed, by U.S. state",
      svg_desc_dis = paste0("Choropleth of the 50 states and DC shaded by the ",
        "share of all working-age people with disabilities who are unemployed ",
        "and looking for work, on a scale shared with the map for people ",
        "without disabilities. Darker is a lower share. Full data is in the ",
        "table below."),
      svg_title_nod = "Share of working-age people without disabilities who are unemployed, by U.S. state",
      svg_desc_nod = paste0("Choropleth of the 50 states and DC on the same ",
        "shared scale for people without disabilities. Full data is in the ",
        "table below."),
      caption = paste0(read_shared, "Darker maroon marks a lower share ",
        "unemployed. This is a share of everyone aged 18 to 64, not the ",
        "unemployment rate; both are in the table. ", src_c18120)),
    ranked = list(
      id = "unemployment", section_heading = "Unemployment, by State",
      intro = paste0("Every state and DC, ranked by the share of all ",
        "working-age people with disabilities who are unemployed. The Tier ",
        "column ranks each state among states with a disability; the maps use ",
        "the pooled scale. The final ",
        "column is the narrower unemployment rate — a share of the labor ",
        "force only — which runs higher."),
      rank_by_col = "emp_unemployed_dis", rank_dir = "low_good",
      tier_col = "tier_unemployed", # self-ranked among states with a disability
      cols = list(
        list(label = "Share unemployed (with disability)",
             value_col = "emp_unemployed_dis", fmt = function(x) fmt_pct(x, 1),
             emphasis = TRUE),
        list(label = "Share unemployed (no disability)",
             value_col = "emp_unemployed_nodis", fmt = function(x) fmt_pct(x, 1)),
        list(label = "Unemployment rate (with disability)",
             value_col = "emp_urate_dis", fmt = function(x) fmt_pct(x, 1))),
      caption = "States ranked by the share of working-age people with disabilities who are unemployed; click a column heading to sort.",
      toggle_label = "Show the 5 lowest and 5 highest",
      restore_label = "Show all 51",
      compare_note = paste0("Tier and map colour answer different questions: the ",
        "Tier column ranks each state only against other states with a disability, ",
        "while the map shades every state on one scale it shares with people ",
        "without disabilities. A state in the top tier here can still sit in a ",
        "pale band on the map &mdash; that distance is the disability gap. The ",
        "unemployment rate (last column) is unemployed people as a share of the ",
        "labor force, not of the whole age group, so it is the larger number.")),
    footnotes = content$unemployment$footnotes)

  vapply(list(employment, nilf, unemployment),
         function(s) build_dual_sheet(s, emp, acs_year), character(1))
}

emp_paths <- build_employment_sheets(emp, acs_year, content)
emp_paths
```
