# Median Earnings factsheet

Built on the simplified single-indicator template (2026-09-07), the same grammar
as the Poverty all-ages lead but with **no age bands**: one takeaway, one
comparative PWD/PWOD dual map on a scale pooled across disability status, Why
This Matters with Key Numbers and a best/worst spotlight, an explainer, and a
searchable ranked table. It joins Poverty in the **Income & Poverty** cluster of
the Work & Economic domain, and is listed before it (earnings is the input, the
poverty rate the outcome).

The indicator is **median individual earnings** from Census table B18140 —
`pop_cni_16plus_medincome_dis` / `_nodis`, in inflation-adjusted survey-year
dollars. It is individual earnings from work, not household income and not total
personal income, and its universe is people aged 16 and older **with earnings**,
so it is silent on the larger share of people with disabilities who are out of
work entirely. Direction is `high_good` (higher earnings = Excellent). The
map's four bands are cut on the with-disability and without-disability series
**pooled**, so a band names position on the shared dollar scale, not rank among
states; the ranked table's Tier column ranks each state among states with a
disability. Legend range chips round to the nearest $1,000.

Puerto Rico follows the Poverty convention: kept off the map, the pooled breaks
and the ranked table, with its figures quoted in the map caption.

```{r medearn-data}
#| label: medearn-data
me_us <- national |> filter(ABBR == "USA")
me_pr <- national |> filter(ABBR == "PR")

me <- states_df |>
  transmute(
    fips, ABBR, name = NAME,
    dis = pop_cni_16plus_medincome_dis,
    nod = pop_cni_16plus_medincome_nodis,
    gap = pop_cni_16plus_medincome_nodis - pop_cni_16plus_medincome_dis
  )
stopifnot(nrow(me) == 51, all(!is.na(c(me$dis, me$nod))), all(me$dis > 0))

# One comparative map on a scale shared across disability status: quartiles of
# the two series pooled, both panels cut on those breaks, one key. PR stays out
# of the pooled vector, as it stays off the map.
me_breaks <- fs_tier_breaks(c(me$dis, me$nod))

me <- me |>
  mutate(
    # pooled tiers for the dual map — position on the shared dollar scale
    ptier_dis = fs_assign_tiers(dis, "high_good", breaks = me_breaks),
    ptier_nod = fs_assign_tiers(nod, "high_good", breaks = me_breaks),
    # self-ranked among the 51 with-disability jurisdictions, for the ranked
    # table's Tier column (the map keeps the pooled scale)
    tier_sr   = fs_assign_tiers(dis, "high_good")
  )

# The two pooled panels are deliberately lopsided — that asymmetry is the
# earnings gap. What must hold is that the two panels together are an equal-count
# split of the 102-value pooled vector. Slack of 2, as in poverty-validate.
me_band_counts <- vapply(
  c("ptier_dis", "ptier_nod"),
  function(col) as.integer(table(factor(me[[col]],
    levels = c("excellent", "above", "below", "poor")))),
  integer(4))
stopifnot(
  "the pooled earnings pair must be an equal-count split across both panels" =
    all(abs(rowSums(me_band_counts) - nrow(me) / 2) <= 2),
  # self-ranked split over 51 jurisdictions must land 13/12/13/13
  "the self-ranked earnings map must be an equal-count quartile split" =
    all(abs(as.integer(table(factor(me$tier_sr,
      levels = c("excellent", "above", "below", "poor")))) - nrow(me) / 4) <= 1)
)

me_values <- c(
  me_dis_us   = fmt_dollars_full(me_us$pop_cni_16plus_medincome_dis),
  me_nod_us   = fmt_dollars_full(me_us$pop_cni_16plus_medincome_nodis),
  me_gap_us   = fmt_dollars_full(me_us$pop_cni_16plus_medincome_nodis -
                                 me_us$pop_cni_16plus_medincome_dis),
  me_ratio_us = formatC(me_us$pop_cni_16plus_medincome_nodis /
                        me_us$pop_cni_16plus_medincome_dis,
                        format = "f", digits = 1)
)
me_values
```

```{r medearn-build}
#| label: medearn-build
build_median_earnings <- function(me, me_us, me_pr, acs_year, cfg, values) {
  usd  <- fmt_dollars_full
  fill <- function(x) fs_assert_no_tokens(
    fs_fill_values(fs_fill_years(unlist(x), acs_year = acs_year), values),
    "median earnings")

  src <- paste0("Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year ",
                "estimates (", acs_year - 4, "&ndash;", acs_year, "), Table B18140.")
  read_shared <- paste0(
    "Both maps use one colour scale, so a shade means the same dollar figure on ",
    "either map, and the distance between them is the earnings gap read straight ",
    "off the colour. The four bands are cut on the two populations pooled. Hover ",
    "or tab through either map for a state's exact figure. ")

  o  <- order(-me$dis)
  bw <- list(best = me[o[1], ], worst = me[o[nrow(me)], ])
  ratio_us <- me_us$pop_cni_16plus_medincome_nodis / me_us$pop_cni_16plus_medincome_dis

  spec <- list(
    id = "median-earnings", out_file = "factsheet-median-earnings.html",
    page_title = "Median Earnings | ADA-PARC Fact Sheet",
    page_desc = paste0("ADA-PARC fact sheet on median earnings among workers ",
      "with disabilities, with state-by-state data."),
    header_title = "Median Earnings",
    header_eyebrow = "ADA-PARC &middot; Work &amp; Economic",
    header_subtitle = "What Workers With Disabilities Earn, Against Workers Without",
    population_note = list(
      note = "Workers aged 16 and older with earnings in the past 12 months",
      detail = paste0("Everyone with no earnings in the past 12 months is outside ",
        "this universe, so the sheet says nothing about people who are out of ",
        "work. People in institutions and correctional facilities, and anyone on ",
        "active military duty, are also excluded.")),
    takeaway = fill(cfg$takeaway),
    why_matters = fill(cfg$intro),
    key_numbers = list(
      list(number = usd(me_us$pop_cni_16plus_medincome_dis),
           label = "median annual earnings for workers with disabilities"),
      list(number = usd(me_us$pop_cni_16plus_medincome_nodis),
           label = "median annual earnings for workers without disabilities"),
      list(number = usd(me_us$pop_cni_16plus_medincome_nodis -
                        me_us$pop_cni_16plus_medincome_dis),
           label = paste0("less a year with a disability, at the median &mdash; ",
             "workers without one earn about ",
             formatC(ratio_us, format = "f", digits = 1),
             "&times; as much"), gap = TRUE)),
    spotlight = list(
      best = list(label = "Highest earnings", state = bw$best$name,
        value = paste0(usd(bw$best$dis),
          " is the median for workers with disabilities"),
        note = paste0("Against ", usd(bw$best$nod),
          " for workers without disabilities in the same state.")),
      worst = list(label = "Lowest earnings", state = bw$worst$name,
        value = paste0(usd(bw$worst$dis),
          " is the median for workers with disabilities"),
        note = paste0("Against ", usd(bw$worst$nod),
          " for workers without disabilities in the same state."))),
    explainer_heading = "What This Map Measures",
    explainer = fill(cfg$earnings_lead),
    map = list(
      id = "median-earnings",
      map_title = "Median Earnings, Workers With and Without Disabilities",
      dis_col = "dis", nod_col = "nod",
      tier_dis_col = "ptier_dis", tier_nod_col = "ptier_nod",
      direction = "high_good", fmt = usd, value_label = "Median earnings",
      pooled_breaks = me_breaks,
      range_fmt = function(v) usd(round(v, -3)),
      legend_best = "highest earnings", legend_worst = "lowest earnings",
      svg_title_dis = "Median earnings among workers with disabilities, by U.S. state",
      svg_desc_dis = paste0("Choropleth of the 50 states and DC shaded by median ",
        "annual earnings among workers with disabilities aged 16 and older, on a ",
        "scale shared with the map for workers without disabilities. Darker is ",
        "higher earnings. Full data is in the table below."),
      svg_title_nod = "Median earnings among workers without disabilities, by U.S. state",
      svg_desc_nod = paste0("Choropleth of the 50 states and DC on the same ",
        "shared scale for workers without disabilities, so this map is broadly ",
        "darker. Full data is in the table below."),
      caption = paste0(read_shared, "Darker maroon marks higher earnings. ",
        "Puerto Rico (with disability ", usd(me_pr$pop_cni_16plus_medincome_dis),
        ", without ", usd(me_pr$pop_cni_16plus_medincome_nodis),
        ") is not shown. ", src)),
    ranked = list(
      id = "median-earnings", section_heading = "Median Earnings, by State",
      intro = paste0("Every state and DC, ranked by median earnings among workers ",
        "with disabilities. The maps above are shaded on one scale pooled with ",
        "workers without disabilities; the Tier column here ranks each state among ",
        "states with a disability. The final column is the dollar gap between the ",
        "two groups. Search, sort, or narrow to the five lowest and five highest."),
      rank_by_col = "dis", rank_dir = "high_good", tier_col = "tier_sr",
      cols = list(
        list(label = "With disability", value_col = "dis", fmt = usd, emphasis = TRUE),
        list(label = "Without disability", value_col = "nod", fmt = usd),
        list(label = "Gap", value_col = "gap", fmt = usd)),
      caption = "States ranked by median earnings among workers with disabilities; click a column heading to sort.",
      toggle_label = "Show the 5 lowest and 5 highest",
      restore_label = "Show all 51",
      compare_note = paste0("Tier and map colour answer different questions: the ",
        "Tier column ranks each state only against other states with a disability, ",
        "while the map shades every state on one scale it shares with workers ",
        "without disabilities. A state in the top tier here can still sit in a ",
        "pale band on the map &mdash; that distance is the earnings gap. The Gap ",
        "column is earnings without a disability minus earnings with one. Puerto ",
        "Rico is not ranked here; its figures are in the map caption.")),
    footnotes = cfg$footnotes)

  build_dual_sheet(spec, me, acs_year)
}

medearn_path <- build_median_earnings(me, me_us, me_pr, acs_year,
                                      content$median_earnings, me_values)
medearn_path
```

```{r medearn-validate}
cat("Pooled-scale band counts (rows = with disability, cols = without), ",

  no_disability   = factor(me$ptier_nod, c("excellent", "above", "below", "poor"))))

cat("\nNational figures behind the Key Numbers:\n")

cat("  without disability: ", fmt_dollars_full(me_us$pop_cni_16plus_medincome_nodis), "\n", sep = "")

                                               me_us$pop_cni_16plus_medincome_dis), "\n", sep = "")

    " / ", fmt_dollars_full(me_pr$pop_cni_16plus_medincome_nodis), "\n", sep = "")
```

# Housing factsheet

Two independent maps (Public Housing, Housing Choice Vouchers), each with its
**own** quartile scale (per-map, not pooled), direction `high_good` (highest
share of heads-of-household with a disability = Excellent). Four tier-grouped
two-column tables per map. DC is labeled "Washington DC" in the tables. Puerto
Rico is appended to the Poor tables **only when present**; in the 2024 vintage
PR has no HUD picture-of-subsidized-households value, so it is omitted.

Variables: `pct_cni_hoh_pubhousing_dis`, `pct_cni_hoh_hcv_dis`.

```{r housing-data}
#| label: housing-data
hd <- states_df |>
  transmute(
    fips, ABBR, name = NAME,
    tname = ifelse(ABBR == "DC", "Washington DC", NAME),
    ph  = pct_cni_hoh_pubhousing_dis,
    hcv = pct_cni_hoh_hcv_dis
  ) |>
  mutate(
    tier_ph  = fs_assign_tiers(ph,  "high_good"),
    tier_hcv = fs_assign_tiers(hcv, "high_good")
  )

ph_breaks  <- fs_tier_breaks(hd$ph)
hcv_breaks <- fs_tier_breaks(hd$hcv)

list(ph = table(hd$tier_ph, useNA = "ifany"),
     hcv = table(hd$tier_hcv, useNA = "ifany"))
```

```{r housing-build}
#| label: housing-build
# Rebuilt on the simplified template (2026-09-01). Public Housing and Housing
# Choice Vouchers are now two single-indicator sheets. Each measure is
# disability-only (share of assisted-housing households headed by someone with a
# disability), so there is no PWD/PWOD pair: a single self-ranked choropleth via
# fs_single_map(), plus the full template furniture and a one-column ranked
# table. Puerto Rico, where a figure exists, is named in the ranked-table
# caption rather than mapped.
build_housing_sheets <- function(hd, pr_row, ph_breaks, hcv_breaks, acs_year, content) {
  pct1 <- function(x) fmt_pct(x, 1)
  eyebrow <- "ADA-PARC &middot; Community Living"

  one <- function(id, out_file, title, subtitle, key, vcol, tcol, brk, prval,
                  value_label, prog_word) {
    o <- order(-hd[[vcol]])
    best <- hd[o[1], ]; worst <- hd[o[nrow(hd)], ]
    pr_note <- if (!is.na(prval)) paste0(" Puerto Rico (", pct1(prval),
      ") is published but not ranked here.") else ""
    spec <- list(
      id = id, out_file = out_file,
      page_title = paste0(title, " | ADA-PARC Fact Sheet"),
      page_desc = paste0("ADA-PARC fact sheet on the share of ", prog_word,
        " households headed by someone with a disability, by state."),
      header_title = title, header_eyebrow = eyebrow, header_subtitle = subtitle,
      population_note = list(
        note = "Assisted households, not people",
        detail = paste0("Percentages are the share of ", prog_word,
          " heads of household who have a disability, so they describe who the ",
          "programme reaches, not what share of people with disabilities are housed.")),
      takeaway = content[[key]]$takeaway,
      why_matters = content[[key]]$intro,
      explainer = content[[key]][[grep("_lead$", names(content[[key]]), value = TRUE)[1]]],
      explainer_heading = "What This Map Measures",
      key_numbers = list(
        list(number = pct1(median(hd[[vcol]], na.rm = TRUE)),
             label = paste0("of ", prog_word, " households are headed by someone with a disability, in the median state")),
        list(number = pct1(min(hd[[vcol]], na.rm = TRUE)), label = "in the lowest state"),
        list(number = pct1(max(hd[[vcol]], na.rm = TRUE)), label = "in the highest state", gap = TRUE)),
      spotlight = list(
        best = list(label = "Highest disability share", state = best$tname,
          value = paste0(pct1(best[[vcol]]), " of ", prog_word, " households headed by someone with a disability"),
          note = "The programme reaches disabled renters at a comparatively high rate here."),
        worst = list(label = "Lowest disability share", state = worst$tname,
          value = paste0(pct1(worst[[vcol]]), " of ", prog_word, " households headed by someone with a disability"),
          note = "A low share can signal barriers to access rather than lower need.")),
      map = list(
        id = id, single = TRUE, map_title = title,
        value_col = vcol, tier_col = tcol, breaks = brk, direction = "high_good",
        fmt = pct1, value_label = value_label,
        legend_best = "highest share", legend_worst = "lowest share",
        svg_title = paste0("Share of ", prog_word,
          " heads of household with a disability, by U.S. state"),
        svg_desc = paste0("Choropleth of the 50 states and DC shaded by the ",
          "share of ", prog_word, " heads of household who have a disability. ",
          "Darker is a higher share. Full data is in the table below."),
        caption = paste0("Darker maroon marks a higher share of ", prog_word,
          " households headed by someone with a disability; states are ranked ",
          "against one another.", pr_note,
          " Source: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, ",
          "A Picture of Subsidized Households.")),
      ranked = list(
        id = id, section_heading = paste0(title, ", by State"),
        intro = paste0("Every state and DC, ranked by the share of ", prog_word,
          " households headed by someone with a disability. Each state's tier is ",
          "its quartile among the states."),
        rank_by_col = vcol, rank_dir = "high_good", tier_col = tcol,
        name_col = "tname",
        cols = list(list(label = "Share with a disability", value_col = vcol,
                         fmt = pct1, emphasis = TRUE)),
        caption = paste0("States ranked by the share of ", prog_word,
          " households headed by someone with a disability; click a column heading to sort."),
        toggle_label = "Show the 5 lowest and 5 highest",
        restore_label = "Show all 51",
        compare_note = paste0("Showing all 50 states and DC by default.", pr_note)),
      footnotes = content[[key]]$footnotes)
    build_dual_sheet(spec, hd, acs_year)
  }

  c(
    one("public-housing", "factsheet-public-housing.html", "Public Housing",
        "Disability Representation Among Public Housing Households",
        "public_housing", "ph", "tier_ph", ph_breaks,
        pr_row$pct_cni_hoh_pubhousing_dis,
        "disability share of public housing", "public housing"),
    one("housing-vouchers", "factsheet-housing-vouchers.html", "Housing Choice Vouchers",
        "Disability Representation Among Housing Choice Voucher Households",
        "housing_vouchers", "hcv", "tier_hcv", hcv_breaks,
        pr_row$pct_cni_hoh_hcv_dis,
        "disability share of Housing Choice Vouchers", "Housing Choice Voucher")
  )
}

housing_paths <- build_housing_sheets(hd, pr_row, ph_breaks, hcv_breaks,
                                      acs_year, content)
housing_paths
```

```{r housing-validate}
#| label: housing-validate
#| echo: false
for (p in housing_paths)
  cat("Wrote: ", p, "  (", file.info(p)$size, " bytes)\n", sep = "")
cat("\nQuartile breaks (self-ranked):\n")
cat("  Public Housing: ",
    paste(formatC(ph_breaks, format = "f", digits = 1), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
cat("  HCV:            ",
    paste(formatC(hcv_breaks, format = "f", digits = 1), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
print(hd |> count(tier_ph,  name = "public_housing"))
print(hd |> count(tier_hcv, name = "housing_vouchers"))
```

# HCBS factsheet

The HCBS factsheet draws on the CMS TAF *Medicaid LTSS Users and Expenditures,
2023* release, **not** the ACS pipeline. Both source files are kept in
`factsheets/_generate/data/` so the generator is self-contained and
reproducible. The indicator (v2) is **HCBS spending per recipient** by state:
total HCBS expenditure from `A2_LTSSExpDlvrySystm_2023.xlsx`, tab
`A.2.3 All-HCBS`, column `HCBS (total)`, divided by the unduplicated count of
HCBS recipients from `A1_LTSSUsrDlvrySystm_2023.xlsx`, tab `A.1.3 All-HCBS`,
column `HCBS (total)`. Both numerator and denominator are "All" (fee-for-service
plus managed care), same source and vintage, so managed-care-heavy states are
represented correctly. Direction is `high_good` (highest spending per recipient
= Excellent); a single map and four dollar-formatted tier tables.

What this measures, and what it does not: per-recipient spending is an
**intensity** measure (dollars per person already receiving HCBS), not a
**reach** measure (whether disabled people can access HCBS at all). A true
per-disabled-enrollee denominator would capture reach, but the TAF release
contains no disabled-Medicaid-enrollee population count, only recipients, so
that variant is deferred to a possible later vintage. The denominator here
covers all HCBS recipients (the large majority are non-elderly disability
groups); a descriptive note on the factsheet reports the subpopulation mix, read
from `C1_LTSSUsrChar_2023.xlsx`, tab `C.1.21 HCBSBySubpop`.

```{r hcbs-data}
#| label: hcbs-data
hcbs_dir <- here::here("factsheets", "_generate", "data")

# Numerator: total HCBS expenditure by state (All = FFS + managed care).
hcbs_spend_raw <- readxl::read_excel(
  file.path(hcbs_dir, "A2_LTSSExpDlvrySystm_2023.xlsx"),
  sheet = "A.2.3 All-HCBS", skip = 1)

# Denominator: unduplicated HCBS recipients by state, same TAF 2023 release.
hcbs_users_raw <- readxl::read_excel(
  file.path(hcbs_dir, "A1_LTSSUsrDlvrySystm_2023.xlsx"),
  sheet = "A.1.3 All-HCBS", skip = 1)

# Institutional expenditure by state, same TAF 2023 release (columns 1 and 2 are
# State and "Institutional (total)"). Used for the community-vs-institutional
# ratio: HCBS / (HCBS + institutional). Because LTSS = HCBS + institutional, this
# equals HCBS as a share of total Medicaid LTSS expenditure.
hcbs_inst_raw <- readxl::read_excel(
  file.path(hcbs_dir, "A2_LTSSExpDlvrySystm_2023.xlsx"),
  sheet = "A.2.2 All-Inst", skip = 1)

# In the HCBS tabs, columns 1 and 2 are State and "HCBS (total)"; in the
# institutional tab they are State and "Institutional (total)". Join spend to
# recipients and institutional spend on state, then attach FIPS via the
# pipeline's NAME (the inner_join drops National + footer rows, leaving 50
# states + DC, no PR/territories).
hcbs <- tibble::tibble(
    name  = hcbs_spend_raw[[1]],
    spend = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(hcbs_spend_raw[[2]]))
  ) |>
  inner_join(
    tibble::tibble(
      name  = hcbs_users_raw[[1]],
      users = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(hcbs_users_raw[[2]]))
    ),
    by = "name"
  ) |>
  inner_join(
    tibble::tibble(
      name       = hcbs_inst_raw[[1]],
      spend_inst = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(hcbs_inst_raw[[2]]))
    ),
    by = "name"
  ) |>
  inner_join(states_df |> select(name = NAME, fips, ABBR), by = "name") |>
  mutate(
    per_recipient = spend / users,
    tier          = fs_assign_tiers(per_recipient, direction = "high_good"),
    # Community share of LTSS spending (0-100). Higher = more community-oriented.
    hcbs_share    = spend / (spend + spend_inst) * 100,
    tier_ratio    = fs_assign_tiers(hcbs_share, direction = "high_good")
  )

# Guard: 51 states, all finite, a wide sanity band on $/recipient, and a valid
# 0-100 community share, so a future vintage with a changed file structure fails
# loudly (observed 2023 ranges: ~$3,600-$48,900 per recipient; ~36%-95% share).
stopifnot(
  nrow(hcbs) == 51,
  all(is.finite(hcbs$per_recipient)),
  all(hcbs$per_recipient > 1000 & hcbs$per_recipient < 75000),
  all(is.finite(hcbs$hcbs_share)),
  all(hcbs$hcbs_share >= 0 & hcbs$hcbs_share <= 100)
)
list(per_recipient = hcbs |> count(tier),
     community_share = hcbs |> count(tier_ratio))
```

```{r hcbs-subpop}
#| label: hcbs-subpop
#| echo: false
# Descriptive context only (not the denominator): national composition of HCBS
# recipients by disability subpopulation, from C1.21 HCBSBySubpop. The "% of
# HCBS" columns are CMS-published shares; groups overlap, so they sum to >100%.
hcbs_subpop_raw <- readxl::read_excel(
  file.path(hcbs_dir, "C1_LTSSUsrChar_2023.xlsx"),
  sheet = "C.1.21 HCBSBySubpop", skip = 1)

hcbs_subpop_natl <- hcbs_subpop_raw[hcbs_subpop_raw[[1]] == "National", ]
sp <- function(col) round(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(hcbs_subpop_natl[[col]])))

# Column order: 2 HCBS total | 3-4 IDD/ASD | 5-6 MH/SUD | 7-8 older adults |
# 9-10 under-65 disabling | 11-12 other (each pair = total, then % of HCBS).
# All five groups are CMS-published shares of HCBS recipients; a person can be
# counted in more than one, so they overlap and sum past 100%.
hcbs_subpop_parts <- c(mh = sp(6), idd = sp(4), u65 = sp(10),
                       old = sp(8), other = sp(12))
hcbs_subpop_other <- if (is.finite(hcbs_subpop_parts[["other"]]) &&
                         hcbs_subpop_parts[["other"]] > 0) {
  paste0(", and another ", hcbs_subpop_parts[["other"]],
         "% are in groups not broken out here")
} else ""
hcbs_subpop_overlap <- if (isTRUE(sum(hcbs_subpop_parts, na.rm = TRUE) > 100)) {
  "People can belong to more than one group, so these shares overlap and sum to more than 100%."
} else {
  "People can belong to more than one group, so these shares overlap."
}
hcbs_subpop_note <- paste0(
  "Among people receiving HCBS nationally, recipients span multiple disability ",
  "groups: about ", sp(6), "% have mental health conditions or substance use ",
  "disorders, ", sp(4), "% have autism, intellectual, or developmental ",
  "disabilities, ", sp(10), "% are adults under 65 with other potentially ",
  "disabling conditions, ", sp(8), "% are older adults", hcbs_subpop_other,
  ". ", hcbs_subpop_overlap)
hcbs_subpop_note
```

```{r hcbs-build}
#| label: hcbs-build
# Rebuilt on the simplified template (2026-09-01). Spending per Recipient and
# the Community Share of LTSS spending are now two single-indicator sheets, each
# a single self-ranked choropleth via fs_single_map() (no PWD/PWOD pair), with
# the Mathematica "About These Data" box carried on both.
build_hcbs_sheets <- function(hcbs, content, acs_year, source_year = 2023,
                              subpop_note = NULL) {
  eyebrow  <- "ADA-PARC &middot; Community Living"
  pr_breaks    <- fs_tier_breaks(hcbs$per_recipient)
  share_breaks <- fs_tier_breaks(hcbs$hcbs_share)
  d0 <- function(x) fmt_dollars_full(x)

  # Legend ranges for spending per recipient are abbreviated to "$NNK". Rounding
  # the outer edges to the nearest $1K can print a floor ABOVE the lowest state
  # ($3,632 -> "$4K"), so the label no longer encloses the data. Floor the
  # minimum break and ceil the maximum; round the interior edges as before.
  pr_range_fmt <- local({
    lo <- min(pr_breaks); hi <- max(pr_breaks)
    function(v) {
      k <- if (isTRUE(all.equal(v, lo))) floor(v / 1000)
           else if (isTRUE(all.equal(v, hi))) ceiling(v / 1000)
           else round(v / 1000)
      paste0("$", formatC(k, format = "d"), "K")
    }
  })

  one <- function(id, out_file, title, subtitle, key, vcol, tcol, brk, fmt,
                  value_label, unit_tail, key_unit, about, extra_why = NULL,
                  range_fmt = NULL) {
    o <- order(-hcbs[[vcol]])
    best <- hcbs[o[1], ]; worst <- hcbs[o[nrow(hcbs)], ]
    spec <- list(
      id = id, out_file = out_file,
      page_title = paste0(title, " | ADA-PARC Fact Sheet"),
      page_desc = paste0("ADA-PARC fact sheet on ", tolower(title),
        " for Medicaid home- and community-based services, by state."),
      header_title = title, header_eyebrow = eyebrow, header_subtitle = subtitle,
      population_note = list(
        note = "State Medicaid HCBS programmes, all waiver types",
        detail = paste0("Figures describe programme dollars, not people. There ",
          "is no comparison population; states are ranked against one another.")),
      takeaway = content[[key]]$takeaway,
      why_matters = c(content[[key]]$intro, extra_why),
      explainer = content[[key]][[grep("_lead$", names(content[[key]]), value = TRUE)[1]]],
      explainer_heading = "What This Map Measures",
      key_numbers = list(
        list(number = fmt(median(hcbs[[vcol]])), label = paste0(key_unit, ", median state")),
        list(number = fmt(min(hcbs[[vcol]])),    label = "in the lowest state"),
        list(number = fmt(max(hcbs[[vcol]])),    label = "in the highest state", gap = TRUE)),
      spotlight = list(
        best = list(label = paste0("Highest ", tolower(value_label)), state = best$name,
          value = paste0(fmt(best[[vcol]]), unit_tail),
          note = "The most community-oriented end of the range."),
        worst = list(label = paste0("Lowest ", tolower(value_label)), state = worst$name,
          value = paste0(fmt(worst[[vcol]]), unit_tail),
          note = "Fewer resources reaching community living here.")),
      map = list(
        id = id, single = TRUE, map_title = title,
        value_col = vcol, tier_col = tcol, breaks = brk, direction = "high_good",
        fmt = fmt, value_label = value_label, range_fmt = range_fmt,
        legend_best = "highest", legend_worst = "lowest",
        svg_title = paste0(title, " for Medicaid HCBS, by U.S. state"),
        svg_desc = paste0("Choropleth of the 50 states and DC shaded by ",
          tolower(title), " for Medicaid home- and community-based services. ",
          "Darker is higher. Full data is in the table below."),
        caption = paste0("Darker maroon marks a higher ", tolower(value_label),
          "; states are ranked against one another. Source: Mathematica for CMS, ",
          "Medicaid LTSS Users &amp; Expenditures, ", source_year,
          " (see About These Data).")),
      ranked = list(
        id = id, section_heading = paste0(title, ", by State"),
        intro = paste0("Every state and DC, ranked by ", tolower(title),
          " for Medicaid HCBS. Each state's tier is its quartile among the states."),
        rank_by_col = vcol, rank_dir = "high_good", tier_col = tcol,
        cols = list(list(label = value_label, value_col = vcol, fmt = fmt, emphasis = TRUE)),
        caption = paste0("States ranked by ", tolower(title),
          "; click a column heading to sort."),
        toggle_label = "Show the 5 lowest and 5 highest",
        restore_label = "Show all 51",
        compare_note = "Showing all 50 states and DC by default."),
      about = about, source_year = source_year,
      footnotes = content[[key]]$footnotes)
    build_dual_sheet(spec, hcbs, acs_year)
  }

  c(
    one("hcbs-spending-per-recipient", "factsheet-hcbs-spending-per-recipient.html",
        "HCBS Spending per Recipient",
        "Medicaid Home- and Community-Based Services Dollars per Person Served",
        "hcbs_spending", "per_recipient", "tier", pr_breaks,
        fmt = d0, value_label = "Spending per recipient",
        unit_tail = " per HCBS recipient", key_unit = "per HCBS recipient",
        about = content$hcbs_spending$about, extra_why = subpop_note,
        range_fmt = pr_range_fmt),
    one("hcbs-community-share", "factsheet-hcbs-community-share.html",
        "Community Share of Long-Term Care Spending",
        "Share of Medicaid Long-Term Care Dollars Going to Home and Community, Not Institutions",
        "hcbs_community_share", "hcbs_share", "tier_ratio", share_breaks,
        fmt = function(x) fmt_pct(x, 1), value_label = "Community share",
        unit_tail = " of Medicaid long-term care spending goes to the community",
        key_unit = "of long-term care spending is community-based",
        about = content$hcbs_community_share$about)
  )
}

hcbs_paths <- build_hcbs_sheets(hcbs, content, acs_year,
                                source_year = 2023, subpop_note = hcbs_subpop_note)
hcbs_paths
```

```{r hcbs-validate}

  cat("Wrote: ", p, "  (", file.info(p)$size, " bytes)\n", sep = "")
cat("\n$/recipient range: ",
    fmt_dollars_full(min(hcbs$per_recipient)), " to ",
    fmt_dollars_full(max(hcbs$per_recipient)), "\n", sep = "")
cat("Community share range: ",
    formatC(min(hcbs$hcbs_share), format = "f", digits = 1), "% to ",
    formatC(max(hcbs$hcbs_share), format = "f", digits = 1), "%\n", sep = "")

print(hcbs |> count(tier_ratio, name = "community_share"))
```

# Health Insurance Access factsheet

Three mapped sections for ages 19 to 64, plus two tables. All eight topics the
National Data tab offers are present; three are mapped and five are tabulated,
for reasons the data forces rather than for space.

**Only "no coverage" is tiered.** It is the one measure on the sheet with a
defensible direction. Public and private coverage are mapped by magnitude with
neutral quartile labels, because a high public share can mean a state has
extended Medicaid widely or that disabled residents are shut out of employer
plans, and the private share carries the mirror-image ambiguity. Tiering either
would assert something the data does not support.

**Covered is not mapped at all.** It is the exact arithmetic complement of no
coverage, so a second map would be the first one inverted. It appears in a table
with both age bands.

**The 65+ band is not mapped.** Medicare makes coverage close to universal, so
across all 51 jurisdictions the uninsured share runs 0.13 to 1.48 percent and
coverage 98.5 to 99.9 percent. Quartiling a spread of roughly one percentage
point would label a state "Poor" for a difference that is not meaningful. Those
four measures appear in a table with a note saying so.

**Public and private overlap.** They exceed the covered total by 7 to 14 points
at ages 19 to 64 and by 40 to 62 points at 65 and over, because a person can
hold both. `fs_hins_measures()` asserts that this overlap is present, so a
future vintage that made the categories exclusive would fail the build rather
than silently invalidate the prose.

```{r hins-data}
#| label: hins-data
hins <- states_df |>
  fs_hins_measures() |>
  mutate(
    name = NAME,
    tier_none    = fs_assign_tiers(hins_none_a19to64_dis,    "low_good"),
    tier_public  = fs_assign_tiers(hins_public_a19to64_dis,  "magnitude"),
    tier_private = fs_assign_tiers(hins_private_a19to64_dis, "magnitude")
  )

# Pooled PWD/PWOD tiers for the simplified template (2026-09-01). Uninsured is
# low_good; public and private coverage keep their magnitude framing.
hins_pooled <- list(
  none    = fs_tier_breaks(c(hins$hins_none_a19to64_dis,    hins$hins_none_a19to64_nodis)),
  public  = fs_tier_breaks(c(hins$hins_public_a19to64_dis,  hins$hins_public_a19to64_nodis)),
  private = fs_tier_breaks(c(hins$hins_private_a19to64_dis, hins$hins_private_a19to64_nodis))
)
hins <- hins |>
  mutate(
    ptier_none_dis    = fs_assign_tiers(hins_none_a19to64_dis,     "low_good",  breaks = hins_pooled$none),
    ptier_none_nod    = fs_assign_tiers(hins_none_a19to64_nodis,   "low_good",  breaks = hins_pooled$none),
    ptier_public_dis  = fs_assign_tiers(hins_public_a19to64_dis,   "magnitude", breaks = hins_pooled$public),
    ptier_public_nod  = fs_assign_tiers(hins_public_a19to64_nodis, "magnitude", breaks = hins_pooled$public),
    ptier_private_dis = fs_assign_tiers(hins_private_a19to64_dis,  "magnitude", breaks = hins_pooled$private),
    ptier_private_nod = fs_assign_tiers(hins_private_a19to64_nodis,"magnitude", breaks = hins_pooled$private)
  )

# Population-weighted national shares. The introduction in
# docs/factsheet-prose.docx quotes 9.9, 12.0, 51.8, 15.0, 49.1 and 76.1 percent
# as typed text; check them against this table when the vintage moves.
hins_national <- local({
  band <- function(an) {
    bd <- hins[[paste0("hins_n_covered_", an, "_dis")]] +
          hins[[paste0("hins_n_none_", an, "_dis")]]
    bn <- hins[[paste0("hins_n_covered_", an, "_nodis")]] +
          hins[[paste0("hins_n_none_", an, "_nodis")]]
    tibble::tibble(
      band    = an,
      measure = c("No coverage", "Covered", "Public", "Private"),
      pwd = vapply(c("none", "covered", "public", "private"), function(m)
        sum(hins[[paste0("hins_n_", m, "_", an, "_dis")]]) / sum(bd) * 100,
        numeric(1)),
      no_disability = vapply(c("none", "covered", "public", "private"), function(m)
        sum(hins[[paste0("hins_n_", m, "_", an, "_nodis")]]) / sum(bn) * 100,
        numeric(1)))
  }
  dplyr::bind_rows(band("a19to64"), band("a65plus"))
})

hins_national |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

```{r hins-build}
#| label: hins-build
# Rebuilt on the simplified template (2026-09-01): three single-indicator sheets
# for ages 19 to 64 — Uninsured (low_good), Public Coverage (magnitude), Private
# Coverage (magnitude). The 65-and-over band and the covered/uninsured
# complement are not mapped (coverage is 1 - uninsured; 65+ is near-universal).
build_hins_sheets <- function(hins, acs_year, content) {
  N   <- hins_national[hins_national$band == "a19to64", ]  # rows: none|covered|public|private
  src <- paste0("Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year ",
    "estimates (", acs_year - 4, "&ndash;", acs_year, "), Table B18135.")
  pop <- "The civilian noninstitutionalized population ages 19 to 64"

  c(
    build_split_sheet("health-insurance-uninsured", "factsheet-health-insurance-uninsured.html",
      "Uninsured", "Working-Age People With Disabilities Who Have No Health Coverage",
      "health_insurance_uninsured", hins,
      "hins_none_a19to64_dis", "hins_none_a19to64_nodis",
      "ptier_none_dis", "ptier_none_nod", "tier_none", "low_good", hins_pooled$none,
      pop, paste0("People 65 and older are outside this universe: Medicare makes ",
        "coverage near-universal at that age, so the sheet stops at 64."),
      "uninsured rate", "of working-age people with disabilities are uninsured",
      key_numbers = list(
        list(number = fmt_pct(N$pwd[1], 1),
             label = "of working-age people with disabilities are uninsured"),
        list(number = fmt_pct(N$no_disability[1], 1),
             label = "of working-age people without disabilities are uninsured"),
        cp_pts_card(N$no_disability[1], N$pwd[1],
          "points lower for people with disabilities &mdash; public programmes fill the gap")),
      spot_labels = c("Lowest uninsured rate", "Highest uninsured rate"),
      acs_year = acs_year, src = src),

    build_split_sheet("health-insurance-public", "factsheet-health-insurance-public.html",
      "Public Health Coverage", "Working-Age People With Disabilities on Medicaid, Medicare or Another Public Plan",
      "health_insurance_public", hins,
      "hins_public_a19to64_dis", "hins_public_a19to64_nodis",
      "ptier_public_dis", "ptier_public_nod", "tier_public", "high_good", hins_pooled$public,
      pop, "Public and private coverage overlap, so the shares are not slices of a whole.",
      "public-coverage share", "of working-age people with disabilities have public coverage",
      key_numbers = list(
        list(number = fmt_pct(N$pwd[3], 1),
             label = "of working-age people with disabilities have public coverage"),
        list(number = fmt_pct(N$no_disability[3], 1),
             label = "of working-age people without disabilities have public coverage"),
        cp_ratio_card(N$pwd[3], N$no_disability[3],
          "as likely to rely on public coverage with a disability")),
      spot_labels = c("Largest public-coverage share", "Smallest public-coverage share"),
      acs_year = acs_year, src = src, magnitude = TRUE),

    build_split_sheet("health-insurance-private", "factsheet-health-insurance-private.html",
      "Private Health Coverage", "Working-Age People With Disabilities Covered by Private, Usually Employer, Insurance",
      "health_insurance_private", hins,
      "hins_private_a19to64_dis", "hins_private_a19to64_nodis",
      "ptier_private_dis", "ptier_private_nod", "tier_private", "high_good", hins_pooled$private,
      pop, "Private and public coverage are not mutually exclusive.",
      "private-coverage share", "of working-age people with disabilities have private coverage",
      key_numbers = list(
        list(number = fmt_pct(N$pwd[4], 1),
             label = "of working-age people with disabilities have private coverage"),
        list(number = fmt_pct(N$no_disability[4], 1),
             label = "of working-age people without disabilities have private coverage"),
        cp_pts_card(N$no_disability[4], N$pwd[4],
          "points lower for people with disabilities")),
      spot_labels = c("Largest private-coverage share", "Smallest private-coverage share"),
      acs_year = acs_year, src = src, magnitude = TRUE)
  )
}

hins_paths <- build_hins_sheets(hins, acs_year, content)
hins_paths
```

```{r hins-validate}
#| label: hins-validate
#| echo: false
for (p in hins_paths)
  cat("Wrote: ", p, "  (", file.info(p)$size, " bytes)\n", sep = "")
cat("\nNational shares (ages 19-64), behind the Key Numbers:\n")
print(hins_national[hins_national$band == "a19to64", ] |>
        mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 1))))
cat("\nPooled-scale band counts (rows = with disability, cols = without):\n")
for (m in c("none", "public", "private")) {
  cat("\n  ", m, "\n", sep = "")
  print(table(
    with_disability = factor(hins[[paste0("ptier_", m, "_dis")]], c("excellent","above","below","poor")),
    no_disability   = factor(hins[[paste0("ptier_", m, "_nod")]], c("excellent","above","below","poor"))))
}
```

# Commuting to Work factsheet

Two mapped sections, both by magnitude, plus a table making the denominator
visible.

**The universe is workers aged 16 and over.** Every percentage on the maps
describes disabled workers, not disabled people. Nationally only 23 percent of
people with disabilities are in that universe, against 51 percent of people
without, so the maps speak for under a quarter of the population the rest of
this fact sheet series covers. That figure is reported in its own table rather
than left implicit.

**Neither mode is tiered.** High transit use can mean accessible transit worth
using or no alternative for someone who cannot drive; high drive-alone can mean
independence or the absence of any usable transit. Both are shaded by magnitude
with neutral quartile labels.

**The two modes do not partition the commute.** Together they account for 55 to
79 percent of journeys depending on the state, with carpooling, walking, cycling
and remote work making up the rest. `fs_commute_measures()` fails the build if a
future vintage ever makes them exhaustive, since the prose describes a remainder.

A note on an assumption that turned out to be wrong. The audit warned that a
state might look strong on transit simply because few of its disabled residents
were employed, making the mode split an artifact of employment. Checked against
this vintage, transit share correlates with the employment rate at **-0.05** and
drive-alone at **-0.12**. The mode split is driven by urban density, not by
employment. What *is* strongly related to employment (+0.93) is the worker share
of the population, which is precisely why it is tabulated separately and pointed
at the Employment sheet rather than folded into the maps.

```{r cm-data}
#| label: cm-data
cm <- states_df |>
  fs_commute_measures() |>
  mutate(
    name = NAME,
    tier_transit    = fs_assign_tiers(cm_transit_dis,    "magnitude"),
    tier_drivealone = fs_assign_tiers(cm_drivealone_dis, "magnitude")
  )

# Pooled PWD/PWOD tiers for the simplified template. Both modes are magnitude:
# neither a high nor a low share is a better outcome for a worker.
cm_pooled <- list(
  transit    = fs_tier_breaks(c(cm$cm_transit_dis,    cm$cm_transit_nodis)),
  drivealone = fs_tier_breaks(c(cm$cm_drivealone_dis, cm$cm_drivealone_nodis))
)
cm <- cm |>
  mutate(
    ptier_transit_dis    = fs_assign_tiers(cm_transit_dis,     "magnitude", breaks = cm_pooled$transit),
    ptier_transit_nod    = fs_assign_tiers(cm_transit_nodis,   "magnitude", breaks = cm_pooled$transit),
    ptier_drivealone_dis = fs_assign_tiers(cm_drivealone_dis,  "magnitude", breaks = cm_pooled$drivealone),
    ptier_drivealone_nod = fs_assign_tiers(cm_drivealone_nodis,"magnitude", breaks = cm_pooled$drivealone)
  )

# Worker-weighted national shares, plus the worker share of each population.
# The introduction in docs/factsheet-prose.docx quotes 23, 51, 3.8 and 65.4
# percent as typed text; check them against this table when the vintage moves.
cm_national <- tibble::tibble(
  measure = c("Commuting workers, share of population",
              "Public transit, share of workers",
              "Drove alone, share of workers"),
  pwd = c(
    sum(cm$cm_workers_dis) / sum(cm$pop_grp_total_dis) * 100,
    sum(cm$pop_cni_16plus_transit_dis)    / sum(cm$cm_workers_dis) * 100,
    sum(cm$pop_cni_16plus_drivealone_dis) / sum(cm$cm_workers_dis) * 100),
  no_disability = c(
    sum(cm$cm_workers_nodis) / sum(cm$pop_grp_total_nodis) * 100,
    sum(cm$pop_cni_16plus_transit_nodis)    / sum(cm$cm_workers_nodis) * 100,
    sum(cm$pop_cni_16plus_drivealone_nodis) / sum(cm$cm_workers_nodis) * 100))

cm_national |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2)))

# The correlations quoted in the prose above, recomputed so a future vintage
# that changes them is visible in the render log rather than silently wrong.
tibble::tibble(
  measure = c("transit share", "drive-alone share", "worker share of population"),
  corr_with_employment_rate = c(
    cor(cm$cm_transit_dis,       cm$pct_cni_18to64_employed_dis),
    cor(cm$cm_drivealone_dis,    cm$pct_cni_18to64_employed_dis),
    cor(cm$cm_worker_share_dis,  cm$pct_cni_18to64_employed_dis))) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

```{r cm-build}
#| label: cm-build
# Rebuilt on the simplified template (2026-09-01): two single-indicator sheets,
# both magnitude (neither a high nor a low mode share is a better outcome). The
# worker share of each population (23% vs 51%) is the key figure on both,
# because the commuting universe is workers only.
build_cm_sheets <- function(cm, acs_year, content) {
  N   <- cm_national   # rows: 1 worker share of pop | 2 transit share | 3 drove-alone share
  src <- paste0("Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year ",
    "estimates (", acs_year - 4, "&ndash;", acs_year, "), Table S1811; universe workers 16+.")
  pop <- "Workers aged 16 and over"
  det <- paste0("Percentages describe how disabled workers travel, not how all ",
    "people with disabilities travel. Only about ", round(N$pwd[1]),
    "% of people with disabilities are commuting workers, against about ",
    round(N$no_disability[1]), "% of people without &mdash; the subject of the ",
    "<em>Employment</em> fact sheet.")
  worker_cards <- function(mode_row, mode_word) list(
    list(number = fmt_pct(N$pwd[1], 0),
         label = "of people with disabilities are commuting workers"),
    list(number = fmt_pct(N$no_disability[1], 0),
         label = "of people without disabilities are commuting workers"),
    list(number = fmt_pct(N$pwd[mode_row], 1),
         label = paste0("of disabled workers ", mode_word), gap = TRUE))

  c(
    build_split_sheet("commuting-transit", "factsheet-commuting-transit.html",
      "Commuting by Public Transit", "Workers With Disabilities Who Travel to Work by Public Transit",
      "commuting_transit", cm,
      "cm_transit_dis", "cm_transit_nodis", "ptier_transit_dis", "ptier_transit_nod",
      "tier_transit", "high_good", cm_pooled$transit, pop, det,
      "transit share of workers", "of workers with disabilities commute by public transit",
      key_numbers = worker_cards(2, "commute by public transit"),
      spot_labels = c("Largest transit share", "Smallest transit share"),
      acs_year = acs_year, src = src, magnitude = TRUE),

    build_split_sheet("commuting-drive-alone", "factsheet-commuting-drive-alone.html",
      "Commuting by Driving Alone", "Workers With Disabilities Who Drive to Work Alone",
      "commuting_drivealone", cm,
      "cm_drivealone_dis", "cm_drivealone_nodis", "ptier_drivealone_dis", "ptier_drivealone_nod",
      "tier_drivealone", "high_good", cm_pooled$drivealone, pop, det,
      "drive-alone share of workers", "of workers with disabilities drive to work alone",
      key_numbers = worker_cards(3, "drive to work alone"),
      spot_labels = c("Largest drive-alone share", "Smallest drive-alone share"),
      acs_year = acs_year, src = src, magnitude = TRUE)
  )
}

cm_paths <- build_cm_sheets(cm, acs_year, content)
cm_paths
```

```{r cm-validate}
#| label: cm-validate
#| echo: false
for (p in cm_paths)
  cat("Wrote: ", p, "  (", file.info(p)$size, " bytes)\n", sep = "")
cat("\nWorker-weighted national shares (behind the Key Numbers):\n")
print(cm_national |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 1))))
cat("\nPooled-scale band counts (rows = with disability, cols = without):\n")
for (m in c("transit", "drivealone")) {
  cat("\n  ", m, "\n", sep = "")
  print(table(
    with_disability = factor(cm[[paste0("ptier_", m, "_dis")]], c("excellent","above","below","poor")),
    no_disability   = factor(cm[[paste0("ptier_", m, "_nod")]], c("excellent","above","below","poor"))))
}
```

# Educational Attainment factsheet

Three mapped sections. A fourth section reporting what the three leave out is
written and tested but held back for the v1 client review; see
`edu_show_remainder` in the build chunk below.

**The three categories are not exhaustive.** Adults whose highest attainment is
some college without a degree, or an associate's degree, fall into none of them.
That is 29 percent of adults with disabilities nationally, so the three
published shares sum to between 63 and 79 percent depending on the state.
`fs_edu_measures()` derives the remainder exactly as 100 less the three, and the
`edu-validate` chunk still checks it on every render, whether or not the sheet
shows it. When `edu_show_remainder` is set back to `TRUE`, the remainder table,
its lead-in, the two introduction paragraphs that describe it and footnote 2 all
return together. Note that while it is hidden the sheet presents three shares
that do not sum to 100 without saying so on the page.

**Directions differ by measure.** Less than high school is low-is-better and
bachelor's or higher is high-is-better; both are tiered. High school or
equivalent is shown by magnitude, because a large share there can mean more
disabled residents finishing high school or more of them stopping at it, and the
data does not distinguish the two.

**A coincidence that looks like a bug.** California reports 23.0 percent both
for "less than high school" and for "bachelor's or higher" among adults with
disabilities, and the derived counts come out bit-identical because they share a
base. This was checked against the aggregate identity: reconstructing the
all-population share from the disabled and non-disabled shares reproduces the
published figure to within 0.06 points on both measures. It is one-decimal
rounding, not a copied value. Four of the 8,407 places in the city file show the
same coincidence. Documented here so nobody re-investigates it.

```{r edu-data}
#| label: edu-data
edu <- states_df |>
  fs_edu_measures() |>
  mutate(
    name = NAME,
    tier_nohs      = fs_assign_tiers(edu_nohs_dis,      "low_good"),
    tier_hs        = fs_assign_tiers(edu_hs_dis,        "magnitude"),
    tier_bachelors = fs_assign_tiers(edu_bachelors_dis, "high_good")
  )

# Pooled PWD/PWOD tiers for the simplified template. Below high school is
# low_good, bachelor's or higher is high_good, high school completion is
# magnitude (it reads two ways at once).
edu_pooled <- list(
  nohs      = fs_tier_breaks(c(edu$edu_nohs_dis,      edu$edu_nohs_nodis)),
  hs        = fs_tier_breaks(c(edu$edu_hs_dis,        edu$edu_hs_nodis)),
  bachelors = fs_tier_breaks(c(edu$edu_bachelors_dis, edu$edu_bachelors_nodis))
)
edu <- edu |>
  mutate(
    ptier_nohs_dis      = fs_assign_tiers(edu_nohs_dis,       "low_good",  breaks = edu_pooled$nohs),
    ptier_nohs_nod      = fs_assign_tiers(edu_nohs_nodis,     "low_good",  breaks = edu_pooled$nohs),
    ptier_hs_dis        = fs_assign_tiers(edu_hs_dis,         "magnitude", breaks = edu_pooled$hs),
    ptier_hs_nod        = fs_assign_tiers(edu_hs_nodis,       "magnitude", breaks = edu_pooled$hs),
    ptier_bachelors_dis = fs_assign_tiers(edu_bachelors_dis,  "high_good", breaks = edu_pooled$bachelors),
    ptier_bachelors_nod = fs_assign_tiers(edu_bachelors_nodis,"high_good", breaks = edu_pooled$bachelors)
  )

# Population-weighted national shares. The introduction in
# docs/factsheet-prose.docx quotes 17.0, 8.9, 20.9, 39.1 and 29 percent as typed
# text; check them against this table when the vintage moves.
edu_national <- tibble::tibble(
  measure = c("Less than high school", "High school or equivalent",
              "Bachelor's degree or higher", "Some college or associate's (derived)"),
  pwd = c(
    sum(edu$pop_cni_25plus_noGED_dis)     / sum(edu$edu_base_dis) * 100,
    sum(edu$pop_cni_25plus_GED_dis)       / sum(edu$edu_base_dis) * 100,
    sum(edu$pop_cni_25plus_bachelors_dis) / sum(edu$edu_base_dis) * 100,
    sum(edu$edu_other_n_dis)              / sum(edu$edu_base_dis) * 100),
  no_disability = c(
    sum(edu$pop_cni_25plus_noGED_nodis)     / sum(edu$edu_base_nodis) * 100,
    sum(edu$pop_cni_25plus_GED_nodis)       / sum(edu$edu_base_nodis) * 100,
    sum(edu$pop_cni_25plus_bachelors_nodis) / sum(edu$edu_base_nodis) * 100,
    NA))

edu_national$no_disability[4] <- 100 - sum(edu_national$no_disability[1:3])
edu_national |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

```{r edu-build}
#| label: edu-build
# Rebuilt on the simplified template (2026-09-01): three single-indicator sheets
# for adults 25 and over — Below High School (low_good), High School Completion
# (magnitude), Bachelor's or Higher (high_good). The "some college / associate's"
# remainder stays deferred (edu_show_remainder), so it is not surfaced here.
edu_show_remainder <- FALSE

build_edu_sheets <- function(edu, acs_year, content) {
  N   <- edu_national   # rows: 1 <HS | 2 HS | 3 bachelor's+ | 4 some-college (derived)
  src <- paste0("Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year ",
    "estimates (", acs_year - 4, "&ndash;", acs_year, "), Table S1811; adults 25+.")
  pop <- "The civilian noninstitutionalized population aged 25 and over"

  c(
    build_split_sheet("education-below-hs", "factsheet-education-below-hs.html",
      "Education Below High School", "Adults With Disabilities Whose Formal Education Ended Before a High School Diploma",
      "education_below_hs", edu,
      "edu_nohs_dis", "edu_nohs_nodis", "ptier_nohs_dis", "ptier_nohs_nod",
      "tier_nohs", "low_good", edu_pooled$nohs, pop,
      "This is the clearest attainment measure and the one most closely tied to later poverty and unemployment.",
      "share without a high school diploma", "of adults with disabilities did not complete high school",
      key_numbers = list(
        list(number = fmt_pct(N$pwd[1], 1),
             label = "of adults with disabilities did not complete high school"),
        list(number = fmt_pct(N$no_disability[1], 1),
             label = "of adults without disabilities did not complete high school"),
        cp_ratio_card(N$pwd[1], N$no_disability[1],
          "as likely to have stopped before high school with a disability")),
      spot_labels = c("Lowest share below high school", "Highest share below high school"),
      acs_year = acs_year, src = src),

    build_split_sheet("education-high-school", "factsheet-education-high-school.html",
      "High School Completion", "Adults With Disabilities Whose Highest Qualification Is a High School Diploma",
      "education_high_school", edu,
      "edu_hs_dis", "edu_hs_nodis", "ptier_hs_dis", "ptier_hs_nod",
      "tier_hs", "high_good", edu_pooled$hs, pop,
      "A large share here can mean a state gets people through high school, or that it does not get them further.",
      "share whose highest qualification is high school",
      "of adults with disabilities stopped at a high school diploma",
      key_numbers = list(
        list(number = fmt_pct(N$pwd[2], 1),
             label = "of adults with disabilities have a high school diploma as their highest qualification"),
        list(number = fmt_pct(N$no_disability[2], 1),
             label = "of adults without disabilities have a high school diploma as their highest qualification"),
        cp_pts_card(N$pwd[2], N$no_disability[2],
          "points higher for people with disabilities")),
      spot_labels = c("Largest share at high school", "Smallest share at high school"),
      acs_year = acs_year, src = src, magnitude = TRUE),

    build_split_sheet("education-bachelors", "factsheet-education-bachelors.html",
      "Bachelor's Degree or Higher", "Adults With Disabilities Holding a Bachelor's Degree or a Higher Qualification",
      "education_bachelors", edu,
      "edu_bachelors_dis", "edu_bachelors_nodis", "ptier_bachelors_dis", "ptier_bachelors_nod",
      "tier_bachelors", "high_good", edu_pooled$bachelors, pop,
      "The state variation reflects both school systems and the accessibility of public universities.",
      "share holding a bachelor's degree or higher",
      "of adults with disabilities hold a bachelor's degree or higher",
      key_numbers = list(
        list(number = fmt_pct(N$pwd[3], 1),
             label = "of adults with disabilities hold a bachelor's degree or higher"),
        list(number = fmt_pct(N$no_disability[3], 1),
             label = "of adults without disabilities hold a bachelor's degree or higher"),
        cp_ratio_card(N$no_disability[3], N$pwd[3],
          "as likely to hold a degree without a disability")),
      spot_labels = c("Highest share with a degree", "Lowest share with a degree"),
      acs_year = acs_year, src = src)
  )
}

edu_paths <- build_edu_sheets(edu, acs_year, content)
edu_paths
```

```{r edu-validate}
#| label: edu-validate
#| echo: false
for (p in edu_paths)
  cat("Wrote: ", p, "  (", file.info(p)$size, " bytes)\n", sep = "")
cat("\nNational attainment shares (behind the Key Numbers):\n")
print(edu_national |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 1))))
cat("\nPooled-scale band counts (rows = with disability, cols = without):\n")
for (m in c("nohs", "hs", "bachelors")) {
  cat("\n  ", m, "\n", sep = "")
  print(table(
    with_disability = factor(edu[[paste0("ptier_", m, "_dis")]], c("excellent","above","below","poor")),
    no_disability   = factor(edu[[paste0("ptier_", m, "_nod")]], c("excellent","above","below","poor"))))
}
```




# Technology Access factsheet

Three maps and three sets of tier tables: the share of people with disabilities
living in a household with a **computer** (`pwd_computer_pct`), an **internet
subscription** (`pwd_int_pct`) and a **smartphone** (`pwd_smartphone_pct`). All
three are `high_good`; there is no reading on which less access is the better
outcome, so none of them is shaded by magnitude. A fourth section puts the three
figures side by side in one alphabetical table, because the tier tables scatter
a single state's three results across three separate boxes and the substitution
of a phone for a computer is only visible when they are read together.

**This sheet is measured differently from every other sheet here, and that is
the thing to know about it.** The other nine read published ACS summary tables
over the civilian noninstitutionalized population. `LAPTOP`, `ACCESSINET` and
`SMARTPHONE` are ACS **housing record** variables with no published table at the
state level, so these figures are tabulated from the Public Use Microdata Sample
with person weights (`PWGTP`). The universe is therefore people with
disabilities **living in occupied housing units**, and everyone in group
quarters is outside it. That is a narrower population than the Community Living
sheets use, which is why the population note says so at the top of the page
rather than in a footnote.

The three indicators share one denominator in every jurisdiction by
construction, because the three questions are asked of the same households. That
identity is the property the July 2026 rebuild exists to restore, and it is
asserted below before anything is built: if it fails, the data is wrong, not the
sheet. See `docs/tech-access-rebuild-plan.qmd` for the defect it replaced and
`scripts/audit_tech_access.R` for the standing acceptance test.

**Puerto Rico.** The quartile breaks are computed over the 51 comparable
jurisdictions, as on every other sheet, and PR is then binned against those same
breaks. It lands in the Poor group on all three measures and sorts to the foot of
that table on its own value. It is not on the maps, because the base map does not
draw it and its figures would set the colour scale for everyone else.

**The PUMS vintage is read from the data, not typed here.** The `{pums_year}` and
`{pums_start}` tokens in the prose are filled from the `adaparc_tech_provenance`
attribute that `national_transform_final.R` attaches to `national_data.Rds`, so a
citation cannot print a year the figures did not come from. `acs_year` is never
used on this sheet.

```{r tech-data}
#| label: tech-data
tech_prov <- attr(national, "adaparc_tech_provenance")

stopifnot(
  "national_data.Rds carries no adaparc_tech_provenance attribute. It predates the PUMS rebuild; re-run national_transform_final.R." =
    !is.null(tech_prov),
  "Technology provenance records no vintage_year" =
    !is.null(tech_prov$vintage_year)
)
pums_year <- as.integer(tech_prov$vintage_year)

# The identity test, restated at the point of use. Recovering each denominator
# by dividing a count by its own percentage is how the original defect was
# found, so the check is done from the published columns rather than trusted
# from upstream. Group quarters residents are outside all three, so the three
# bases must agree to within rounding in every jurisdiction.
tech_universe <- national |>
  filter(!ABBR %in% "USA") |>
  transmute(
    ABBR,
    den_computer   = pwd_computer   / (pwd_computer_pct   / 100),
    den_internet   = pwd_int        / (pwd_int_pct        / 100),
    den_smartphone = pwd_smartphone / (pwd_smartphone_pct / 100),
    spread = pmax(den_computer, den_internet, den_smartphone) -
             pmin(den_computer, den_internet, den_smartphone))

stopifnot(
  "The three technology indicators do not share a denominator. Do not publish this sheet; see docs/tech-access-rebuild-plan.qmd section 8." =
    all(tech_universe$spread / tech_universe$den_computer < 0.001)
)

# 51 comparable jurisdictions set the scale; Puerto Rico is binned against it.
tech_states <- states_df |>
  transmute(
    fips, ABBR, name = NAME,
    computer   = pwd_computer_pct,   n_computer   = pwd_computer,
    internet   = pwd_int_pct,        n_internet   = pwd_int,
    smartphone = pwd_smartphone_pct, n_smartphone = pwd_smartphone,
    computer_nod   = pwod_computer_pct,
    internet_nod   = pwod_int_pct,
    smartphone_nod = pwod_smartphone_pct)

tech_breaks <- lapply(c(computer = "computer", internet = "internet",
                        smartphone = "smartphone"),
                      function(v) fs_tier_breaks(tech_states[[v]]))

# fips is NA for Puerto Rico, which is what keeps it off the maps;
# fs_indicator_section() drops rows the base map cannot draw. It is binned
# against the breaks computed above rather than changing them, and it sorts to
# the foot of its tier table on its own value like any other row.
tech_pr <- national |>
  filter(ABBR == "PR") |>
  transmute(
    fips = NA_character_, ABBR, name = NAME,
    computer   = pwd_computer_pct,   n_computer   = pwd_computer,
    internet   = pwd_int_pct,        n_internet   = pwd_int,
    smartphone = pwd_smartphone_pct, n_smartphone = pwd_smartphone,
    computer_nod   = pwod_computer_pct,
    internet_nod   = pwod_int_pct,
    smartphone_nod = pwod_smartphone_pct)

# Pooled PWD/PWOD breaks for the simplified template (51 jurisdictions only; PR
# is binned against them, as with the self-ranked breaks above).
tech_pooled <- lapply(
  c(computer = "computer", internet = "internet", smartphone = "smartphone"),
  function(v) fs_tier_breaks(c(tech_states[[v]], tech_states[[paste0(v, "_nod")]])))

tech <- bind_rows(tech_states, tech_pr) |>
  mutate(
    tier_computer   = fs_assign_tiers(computer,   "high_good", tech_breaks$computer),
    tier_internet   = fs_assign_tiers(internet,   "high_good", tech_breaks$internet),
    tier_smartphone = fs_assign_tiers(smartphone, "high_good", tech_breaks$smartphone),
    ptier_computer_dis   = fs_assign_tiers(computer,       "high_good", tech_pooled$computer),
    ptier_computer_nod   = fs_assign_tiers(computer_nod,   "high_good", tech_pooled$computer),
    ptier_internet_dis   = fs_assign_tiers(internet,       "high_good", tech_pooled$internet),
    ptier_internet_nod   = fs_assign_tiers(internet_nod,   "high_good", tech_pooled$internet),
    ptier_smartphone_dis = fs_assign_tiers(smartphone,     "high_good", tech_pooled$smartphone),
    ptier_smartphone_nod = fs_assign_tiers(smartphone_nod, "high_good", tech_pooled$smartphone))

# National figures, for checking the numbers quoted in docs/factsheet-prose.docx
# when the vintage moves. The introduction types 72.8, 86.2, 89.6, 96.6, 85.2,
# 95.2, 13.4, 12.4, 22.8 and 11.7 million as fixed text.
usa_row  <- national |> filter(ABBR == "USA")
usa_base <- usa_row$pwd_computer / (usa_row$pwd_computer_pct / 100)

tech_national <- tibble::tibble(
  measure  = c("Computer", "Internet", "Smartphone"),
  pwd      = c(usa_row$pwd_computer_pct,  usa_row$pwd_int_pct,  usa_row$pwd_smartphone_pct),
  nodis    = c(usa_row$pwod_computer_pct, usa_row$pwod_int_pct, usa_row$pwod_smartphone_pct),
  have     = c(usa_row$pwd_computer, usa_row$pwd_int, usa_row$pwd_smartphone)) |>
  mutate(gap = nodis - pwd, lack = usa_base - have)

list(pums_vintage = tech_prov$vintage_label,
     national = tech_national |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))),
     tiers = lapply(tech[c("tier_computer", "tier_internet", "tier_smartphone")],
                    table, useNA = "ifany"))
```

```{r tech-build}
#| label: tech-build
# Rebuilt on the simplified template (2026-09-01): three single-indicator sheets
# — Computer, Internet, Smartphone — all high_good, all comparative PWD/PWOD
# dual maps on a pooled scale. PUMS vintage, so footnotes carry {pums_*} tokens.
# Puerto Rico is binned against the 51-jurisdiction scale but not mapped or
# ranked; its rate is noted in the ranked-table caption.
build_tech_sheets <- function(tech, pums_year, content) {
  N   <- tech_national   # rows: 1 computer | 2 internet | 3 smartphone; cols pwd/nodis/gap/lack
  ts  <- tech[!is.na(tech$fips), ]
  pr  <- tech[tech$ABBR == "PR", ]
  src <- paste0("Source: U.S. Census Bureau, ACS 5-year Public Use Microdata ",
    "Sample (", pums_year - 4, "&ndash;", pums_year, "). ")

  one <- function(id, out_file, title, subtitle, key, row, dis_col, nod_col,
                  tdis, tnod, brk, unit_word, key3) {
    prval <- pr[[dis_col]]
    pr_note <- if (length(prval) == 1 && !is.na(prval))
      paste0(" Puerto Rico (", fmt_pct(prval, 1), ") is not mapped or ranked here.") else ""
    sheet_src <- paste0(src, "Differences between states of less than about one ",
      "percentage point should not be read as real.", pr_note)
    build_split_sheet(id, out_file, title, subtitle, key, ts,
      dis_col, nod_col, tdis, tnod, paste0("tier_", dis_col), "high_good", brk,
      "People with disabilities living in occupied housing units",
      "Residents of nursing homes, group homes and other group quarters are outside this universe, so it is narrower than the Living in Community population.",
      paste0("share living in a household with a ", unit_word),
      paste0("of people with disabilities live in a household with a ", unit_word),
      key_numbers = key3, spot_labels = c(paste0("Highest ", unit_word, " access"),
        paste0("Lowest ", unit_word, " access")),
      acs_year = pums_year, src = sheet_src, pums_year = pums_year)
  }

  c(
    one("technology-computer", "factsheet-technology-computer.html",
      "Computer Access", "People With Disabilities Living in a Household With a Laptop or Desktop Computer",
      "technology_computer", 1, "computer", "computer_nod",
      "ptier_computer_dis", "ptier_computer_nod", tech_pooled$computer, "computer",
      key3 = list(
        list(number = fmt_pct(N$pwd[1], 1), label = "of people with disabilities live in a household with a computer"),
        list(number = fmt_pct(N$nodis[1], 1), label = "of people without disabilities live in a household with a computer"),
        list(number = fmt_count(N$lack[1]), label = "people with disabilities live in a household with no computer at all", gap = TRUE))),

    one("technology-internet", "factsheet-technology-internet.html",
      "Internet Access", "People With Disabilities Living in a Household With an Internet Subscription",
      "technology_internet", 2, "internet", "internet_nod",
      "ptier_internet_dis", "ptier_internet_nod", tech_pooled$internet, "internet subscription",
      key3 = list(
        list(number = fmt_pct(N$pwd[2], 1), label = "of people with disabilities have a household internet subscription"),
        list(number = fmt_pct(N$nodis[2], 1), label = "of people without disabilities have a household internet subscription"),
        list(number = paste0(formatC(N$gap[2], format = "f", digits = 1), " pts"),
             label = "lower for people with disabilities &mdash; the smallest of the three technology gaps", gap = TRUE))),

    one("technology-smartphone", "factsheet-technology-smartphone.html",
      "Smartphone Access", "People With Disabilities Living in a Household With a Smartphone",
      "technology_smartphone", 3, "smartphone", "smartphone_nod",
      "ptier_smartphone_dis", "ptier_smartphone_nod", tech_pooled$smartphone, "smartphone",
      key3 = list(
        list(number = fmt_pct(N$pwd[3], 1), label = "of people with disabilities live in a household with a smartphone"),
        list(number = fmt_pct(N$nodis[3], 1), label = "of people without disabilities live in a household with a smartphone"),
        list(number = paste0(formatC(N$pwd[3] - N$pwd[1], format = "f", digits = 1), " pts"),
             label = "more people with disabilities have a smartphone than have a computer", gap = TRUE)))
  )
}

tech_paths <- build_tech_sheets(tech, pums_year, content)
tech_paths
```

```{r tech-validate}
#| label: tech-validate
#| echo: false
for (p in tech_paths)
  cat("Wrote: ", p, "  (", file.info(p)$size, " bytes)\n", sep = "")
cat("\nPUMS vintage: ", tech_prov$vintage_label, "\n", sep = "")
cat("\nNational figures (behind the Key Numbers):\n")
print(tech_national |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 1))))
cat("\nPooled-scale band counts, 51 jurisdictions (rows = with disability, cols = without):\n")
for (m in c("computer", "internet", "smartphone")) {
  cat("\n  ", m, "\n", sep = "")
  ts <- tech[!is.na(tech$fips), ]
  print(table(
    with_disability = factor(ts[[paste0("ptier_", m, "_dis")]], c("excellent","above","below","poor")),
    no_disability   = factor(ts[[paste0("ptier_", m, "_nod")]], c("excellent","above","below","poor"))))
}
cat("\nPuerto Rico (off the maps, noted in captions):\n")
print(tech[tech$ABBR == "PR", c("name", "computer", "internet", "smartphone")])
```
